question: How far is Boerne from San Antonio?
metaTitle: How far is Boerne from San Antonio?
metaDescription: About 31 miles northwest on I-10, 30 to 45 minutes downtown, and Kendall County rather than Bexar, so a different appraisal district applies.
shortAnswer: Boerne is roughly 31 miles northwest of San Antonio on Interstate 10, a 30-to-45-minute drive to downtown depending on traffic. Boerne is the county seat of Kendall County, not part of the City of San Antonio and not in Bexar County, so different ordinances and a different appraisal district apply.
body:
## The distance

**About 31 miles, northwest, on I-10** ([City-Data, Boerne](https://www.city-data.com/city/Boerne-Texas.html)). Boerne's ZIP codes are 78006 and 78015. City Hall is at 201 East San Antonio Avenue, Boerne, TX 78006.

Thirty-one miles is the straightforward part of the answer. The rest of this page is about what that distance does and does not buy you.

## Drive time is not a single number

**30 to 45 minutes to downtown San Antonio, depending on traffic.** The spread is the useful information, not the midpoint.

I-10 southbound out of Boerne runs clean until it meets the Loop 1604 interchange and the growth on the northwest side of Bexar County. That is where the variance lives. The same trip is a different trip at 7:15 a.m. than at 10:00 a.m., and a different trip again on a Friday afternoon.

Practical advice that costs nothing: before you make an offer, drive the exact route from the exact house at the exact hour you would actually leave. Twice. A commute you can tolerate on a Saturday tour is not the commute you bought.

Where in San Antonio you work matters as much as the mileage. The I-10 corridor and the northwest side are the easy version of this commute. The far east or south side of Bexar County is a materially longer trip than "31 miles" suggests, because you cross the whole metro to get there.

## Boerne is not a San Antonio suburb in the legal sense

This is the part that costs people money.

Boerne is an **incorporated city and the county seat of Kendall County**. San Antonio is in **Bexar County**. The consequences:

- **Your appraisal district is [Kendall Appraisal District](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/), not Bexar CAD.** Homestead exemption applications and appraisal protests go to Kendall AD. A buyer relocating from a San Antonio address who files with Bexar CAD out of habit can lose the exemption for that tax year, and the Texas exemption deadline is **before May 1**, with the owner required to have **owned and occupied the home as of January 1** ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)).
- **San Antonio ordinances do not govern Boerne.** The clearest example is short-term rentals: Boerne regulates STRs under its **own Ordinance No. 2023-09**, with its own permit fee, inspection rule, insurance minimum and block-face spacing requirement ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/2444/Short-Term-Rentals)). Researching San Antonio's STR rules and then buying in Boerne means reading the wrong rulebook.
- **Your taxing units are different.** The 2025 adopted rates per $100 of taxable value inside the city limits are **Boerne ISD 1.0109**, split 0.6969 M&O and 0.3140 debt ([Kendall County](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/295/Boerne-ISD)); **City of Boerne 0.4716** ([Kendall County](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/297/Boerne-City-of)); and **Kendall County 0.377** ([Kendall County](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/306/Kendall-County)). Any special district on the parcel adds its own line.
- **Sales tax is 8.25 percent** — 6.25 percent state, 1.50 percent City of Boerne, 0.50 percent Kendall County ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/646/Current-Tax-Rates)). Same total as much of San Antonio, different recipients.
- **Schools are Boerne ISD**, not Northside ISD or any other Bexar County district.

"Thirty minutes from San Antonio" is a commute description. It is not a statement about which government you live under.

## What sits between the two

The corridor between Boerne and San Antonio is not empty, and the towns in it are governed differently from each other too.

**Fair Oaks Ranch** sits on that northwest edge. It incorporated in **1988**, had a **2020 census population of 9,833**, and — the detail that catches people — its **city limits span Bexar, Comal and Kendall counties** ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_Oaks_Ranch,_Texas)). Two Fair Oaks Ranch addresses can answer to two different appraisal districts.

**Bulverde** is on the other corridor entirely — **Comal County, incorporated 1999, 2020 population 5,692, served by Comal ISD, with US 281 running through the east side** ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulverde,_Texas)). It is closer to San Antonio's north-central employment, farther from I-10.

If your search is really "somewhere 30 minutes out of San Antonio," those are your other two candidates, and they are not interchangeable with Boerne on taxes, schools or jurisdiction.

## Distance in the other direction

Boerne's distance from San Antonio is also what people are buying. It is far enough that the town has its own downtown, its own school district and its own county government, and near enough that a San Antonio job, a San Antonio hospital and a San Antonio airport are an ordinary drive rather than an expedition.

Towns that are only near — bedroom subdivisions with no independent center — do not hold value the same way. Towns that are only far do not draw the commuting household. Boerne is on both sides of that line, and that is priced in.

## Before you commit to the commute

- Drive it live, at your real hours, in both directions.
- Check the specific address against the actual employer location, not against "San Antonio."
- Confirm the parcel's county and taxing units on the appraisal record, not on the listing sheet.
- If the property is outside city limits, confirm whether it is in Boerne's extraterritorial jurisdiction with the **City of Boerne Planning Department**, because some city rules reach into the ETJ.

## Related questions

- [Is Boerne, Texas a good place to live?](/answers/is-boerne-texas-a-good-place-to-live)
- [Boerne vs. Fair Oaks Ranch vs. Bulverde: which should I buy in?](/answers/boerne-vs-fair-oaks-ranch-vs-bulverde)

question: How much down payment do I need to buy a house in Texas?
metaTitle: How much down payment do I need to buy a house in Texas?
metaDescription: Down payment in Texas: how loan program, occupancy and homestead status set the number, and what cash you need at closing besides the down payment.
shortAnswer: How much you put down depends on the loan program, whether the home will be your homestead or an investment property, and what your lender's overlay requires. Conventional, FHA and VA each set different minimums, and a veteran with full entitlement has no VA loan limit. Only a lender preapproval gives you a real number.
body:
## The number is set by four things, in this order

1. **The loan program.** Conventional, FHA, VA and USDA each have their own minimum. They are not close to each other, and a borrower is frequently eligible for more than one.
2. **What you are doing with the property.** A primary residence, a second home and an investment property are underwritten as three different risks by every program that allows them at all. Occupancy is the single largest swing in the required down payment, larger than credit score.
3. **The lender's overlay.** The program floor is what the agency will accept. The overlay is what the lender in front of you will actually do. Overlays are unpublished and vary between lenders on the same day.
4. **The property type.** One unit versus two to four units, condominium versus single family, manufactured versus site-built — each moves the requirement.

Anyone who answers this question with a percentage before asking those four things is quoting a marketing number.

## Homestead versus everything else in Texas

Texas has a specific legal category for the home you actually live in: the **homestead**. It is the basis for the residence homestead exemption on your property taxes, and it is the trigger for the constitutional limits on borrowing against your own house.

The homestead distinction shows up in three places a buyer feels:

- **Financing terms.** Owner-occupied financing is materially cheaper and requires less down than non-owner-occupied financing. Occupancy is a representation you make to the lender, in writing, under penalty. Telling a lender you will occupy a property you intend to rent out is mortgage fraud, not a strategy.
- **Property taxes.** A residence homestead exemption requires that you **owned and occupied the home as your principal residence on January 1** of the tax year, and the application is filed **before May 1** with the county appraisal district ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)). For a Boerne home that is the **Kendall Appraisal District**, not Bexar CAD — Boerne is in Kendall County, not the City of San Antonio.
- **Getting equity back out later.** A cash-out refinance or home equity loan on a Texas homestead is governed by the **Texas Constitution, Section 50(a)(6)**: all loans against the homestead combined cannot exceed **80% of fair market value**, meaning at least 20% equity must remain; the loan cannot close until at least **12 days** after the later of application or your receipt of the required notice; fees other than appraisal, survey, title insurance premium and title search/exam are capped at **2%** of principal; the loan is generally **non-recourse**; and you may have only **one** at a time, with **12 months** between home equity closings ([Texas cash-out rules summarized](https://hurstlending.com/texas-cash-out-refinance-rules-50a6-guidelines/)).

That last point is the one buyers in other states get wrong. If your plan is to put very little down and then pull cash out in two years, Texas law caps the total at 80% of value on the homestead. Investment property in Texas is **not** governed by 50(a)(6).

## The VA case is genuinely different

A veteran with **full entitlement has no VA loan limit**, and the VA guaranty does not exceed 25% of the loan ([U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs](https://www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans/loan-limits/)). "No limit" means the VA does not cap the loan amount for a veteran with full entitlement — it does not mean a lender will lend any amount. The lender still underwrites income, assets, credit and the appraisal.

Entitlement is not automatically full. A veteran with an existing VA loan, or one who previously had a VA loan foreclosed on, may have partial entitlement, and that changes the math. The Certificate of Eligibility settles it, and the lender pulls it.

## What has to be in the bank besides the down payment

The down payment is one of four cash requirements, and buyers routinely budget for only the first.

**Option fee and earnest money.** In Texas both are due early. The option fee goes to the escrow agent — the title company, not the seller — **within three days after the effective date** of the contract, and if day three falls on a weekend or legal holiday it rolls to the next business day ([TREC](https://www.trec.texas.gov/article/changes-delivery-option-fee-0)). Earnest money goes to the same escrow agent. The option fee is credited to the sales price at closing; it is not refunded if you terminate. Amounts are negotiated, not set by law.

**Inspection and due diligence costs.** Paid out of pocket during the option period, before you know whether you are buying the house. On a Hill Country property that can mean a general inspection plus a septic inspection, a well test, and a structural or foundation opinion. None of it is financed.

**Closing costs.** Separate from the down payment. Who pays what is **negotiated in the contract, not fixed by law**. Custom in much of Texas is that the seller pays for the owner's title policy; in some markets the buyer does. Texas title insurance premium rates are **promulgated by the Texas Department of Insurance**, which means the premium for a given policy amount is identical at every title company in the state — you are not going to shop your way to a cheaper policy ([TDI title rates](https://tdi.texas.gov/title/titlerates2026.html), schedule effective March 1, 2026).

**Reserves.** Many loan programs and most lender overlays require documented reserves after closing — months of principal, interest, taxes and insurance still sitting in an account. A borrower who drains every account to hit the down payment can fail the reserve test and lose the approval.

## Gift funds, and the paper trail

Gift funds are allowed on most programs, with conditions: an acceptable donor relationship, a gift letter stating the funds do not have to be repaid, and a documented transfer. The failure mode is almost never the gift itself. It is the paper trail — cash deposited at a branch, money moved between three accounts before it lands, or funds appearing after the application without an explanation. Underwriters call these unsourced deposits and they will stop a file cold. Move money once, in a traceable way, and tell the loan officer before you do it.

## Why a real preapproval is the only number worth planning around

A calculator on a lender's website does not know your debt, your documented income, the property, or that lender's overlay. A preapproval where credit has been pulled and income and asset documents have actually been read produces a number you can plan against, and a letter a listing agent will take seriously. On the contract side, a buyer whose purchase depends on financing uses the **Third Party Financing Addendum, TREC form 40-11, effective 01/03/2025** ([TREC contract forms](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/contracts)). That addendum and your preapproval are what the seller's side weighs against the other offer on the table.

## Who to ask

Program minimums, overlays, entitlement, reserve requirements and what your specific file supports are **lender** questions. Homestead exemption filing and deadlines go to the **Kendall Appraisal District** for a Boerne or Kendall County property. How the Texas homestead rules apply to your ownership situation, including anything involving marital property or title, is a question for a **Texas real estate attorney**.

## Related questions

- [What credit score do I need to buy a house in Texas?](/answers/what-credit-score-do-i-need-to-buy-a-house-in-texas)
- [Conventional vs. FHA vs. VA loan in Texas: which one?](/answers/conventional-vs-fha-vs-va-loan-in-texas)
- [What are the 2026 conforming and FHA loan limits in Kendall County, Texas?](/answers/what-are-the-2026-loan-limits-in-kendall-county)
- [Who pays closing costs in Texas?](/answers/who-pays-closing-costs-in-texas)
- [What is a Texas cash-out refinance (50(a)(6))?](/answers/what-is-a-texas-cash-out-refinance-50a6)

## Questions about a specific property?

Call or text **[830-446-3847](tel:+1-830-446-3847)** · Email **[heath.shepard@kw.com](mailto:heath.shepard@kw.com)**

question: Is Boerne, Texas a good real estate investment?
metaTitle: Is Boerne, Texas a good real estate investment?
metaDescription: Kendall County grew 20.3 percent since 2020, but a 1.8595 combined tax rate and the December 2026 circuit-breaker sunset compress Boerne cash flow.
shortAnswer: Boerne's fundamentals support long-term value: 20.3 percent Kendall County population growth from 2020 to 2025 driven by domestic migration, six straight A ratings for Boerne ISD, and land and groundwater constraints that limit new supply. Cash flow is the hard part, because Texas property tax rates and Hill Country prices compress yields.
body:
## The appreciation case, stated in verifiable terms

**Demand.** **Kendall County grew 20.3 percent between 2020 and 2025**, from an estimated 44,568 to 53,289 residents, and the growth came mostly from **domestic migration** ([Community Impact](https://communityimpact.com/san-antonio/boerne-fair-oaks-ranch/government/2026/03/30/kendall-county-population-increases-by-203-from-2020-2025/)). In-migrating households form demand immediately and arrive with prior-sale equity.

**Sorting pressure.** **Boerne ISD has held a Texas Education Agency "A" rating for six consecutive years** ([Boerne Star](https://www.boernestar.com/article/11432,boerne-isd-six-straight-years-of-a-ratings)). School ratings are the primary filter relocating families apply before they look at a listing, and that filter concentrates demand inside district boundaries.

**Constrained supply.** Hill Country terrain limits finished-lot yield per acre, and groundwater across Kendall County is regulated by the **Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District** ([ccgcd.org](https://ccgcd.org/)). A project that cannot document water does not get built at the density its pro forma assumed. Rising demand against constrained supply is the whole appreciation thesis.

**Access.** Boerne sits roughly **31 miles northwest of San Antonio on I-10** ([City-Data](https://www.city-data.com/city/Boerne-Texas.html)) — commutable to a metro job market while remaining a separate town with its own downtown, county government and school district.

None of those four reverse quickly. That is what "fundamentals" means.

## The cash flow problem, stated honestly

Appreciation and cash flow are different businesses. Boerne is better at the first than the second, and the reason is on the tax bill.

For a home inside the city limits in Boerne ISD, the **2025 adopted rates per $100 of taxable value** were:

- **Boerne ISD 1.0109** — 0.6969 M&O plus 0.3140 debt ([Kendall County](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/295/Boerne-ISD))
- **City of Boerne 0.4716** ([Kendall County](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/297/Boerne-City-of))
- **Kendall County 0.377** — 0.317976 M&O plus 0.059024 debt ([Kendall County](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/306/Kendall-County))

Plus any special district on the parcel. Kendall AD lists Kendall County MUD, Miralomas MUD, Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District and Kendall County WCID #1 among entities that can appear on a bill ([Kendall Appraisal District](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)).

Two consequences investors miss:

1. **An investment property gets no homestead exemption and no 10 percent homestead cap.** The 10 percent cap on annual increases in net appraised value applies only to property that already carries a homestead exemption ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)). Your rental is reappraised at market value with no such cushion.
2. **The partial substitute is expiring.** The **circuit breaker** in Tax Code §23.231 caps appraised value increases at **20 percent per year for non-homestead real property** at or below an annually indexed threshold. It was created by **SB 2 (2023)** as a pilot for tax years **2024, 2025 and 2026, and it expires December 31, 2026** unless the Legislature renews it ([Travis CAD](https://traviscad.org/circuitbreaker)). It excludes land under agricultural special appraisal and homesteads under the 10 percent cap. An investor underwriting a Boerne rental on 2026 assessed value should model what happens if that cap lapses. A **CPA or tax advisor** is the right person to run that scenario.

On the price side, published Boerne figures are third-party model estimates that move. Zillow reported an average Boerne home value of roughly **$554,983 as of September 2026** ([Zillow](https://www.zillow.com/home-values/8154/boerne-tx/)) — not a closed-sale statistic. Get current MLS sold and rent comps for the specific ZIP and property type before underwriting anything.

## The short-term rental angle, and its ceiling

Boerne is a destination town, which makes nightly rental the obvious yield play. It is also regulated. **Boerne has its own ordinance — No. 2023-09 — and San Antonio's STR rules do not apply here.** Key terms: **$200 registration fee, two-year permit term, $200 renewal within 30 days of expiration, safety inspection required inside city limits ($100 with a city inspector) but not in the ETJ, minimum liability insurance of $500,000 per occurrence and $1,000,000 aggregate, occupancy of two per bedroom plus two, one parking space per bedroom, events prohibited**, and — the deal-killer — **an STR may not operate within 200 feet of another STR on the same block face in residentially zoned areas** ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/2444/Short-Term-Rentals)).

**Hotel occupancy tax is 13 percent combined: 6 percent state plus 7 percent City of Boerne** ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/646/Current-Tax-Rates)).

The failure mode is specific: an investor buys the block closest to the Hill Country Mile because the nightly rate justifies the price, then discovers the block-face allowance is already consumed by an existing permit holder. Confirm the specific address with the **City of Boerne Planning Department, (830) 248-1501**, inside the option period. And a city permit is not a POA's permission — deed restrictions are a separate question for a **Texas real estate attorney**.

## Land plays are a different instrument

Raw Hill Country acreage does not cash flow, and untaxed it carries a real holding cost. **1-d-1 open-space appraisal** values qualifying land on **productivity value** rather than market value, and requires current principal agricultural use to the degree of intensity generally accepted in the area, with agricultural or timber production in **5 of the preceding 7 years**. **Wildlife management use** requires previously qualified open-space or timber land used in **at least 3 of 7** specified ways. Changing use triggers a **3-year rollback tax** — the difference between taxes paid on ag value and what would have been paid on market value ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/ag-timber/index.php)).

Buying ag-valued land and developing it converts a low carrying cost into a rollback liability. That math belongs to a **CPA**, and the qualification question belongs to **Kendall Appraisal District**.

## If you are exchanging in

**IRC §1031** allows deferral on real property held for productive use in a trade or business or for investment. After the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act it applies **only to real property**. The clocks: **45 days** from transfer of the relinquished property to identify replacement property in writing, and **180 days** to receive it, **or the due date of the return including extensions, whichever is earlier**. Reported on **IRS Form 8824**. A **personal residence does not qualify** ([IRS](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/like-kind-exchanges-real-estate-tax-tips)). Work with a CPA and a qualified intermediary before the relinquished property closes, not after.

## The honest verdict

Buy Boerne for a long hold, for land you cannot replace, or for a resale-price thesis backed by school ratings and in-migration. Do not buy it expecting a Midwest cap rate. And run the tax line at full market value with no exemption before you sign anything — that is the number that kills Hill Country pro formas.

## Related questions

- [Why are homes in Boerne, Texas so expensive?](/answers/why-are-homes-in-boerne-so-expensive)
- [Short-Term Rental Rules in Boerne, TX](/boerne/boerne-tx-short-term-rental-rules)
- [What are property taxes like in Boerne, Texas?](/answers/what-are-property-taxes-like-in-boerne)
- [Is Boerne, Texas growing?](/answers/is-boerne-texas-growing)
- [Is Hill Country land a good investment?](/answers/is-hill-country-land-a-good-investment)

## Questions about a specific property?

Call or text **[830-446-3847](tel:+1-830-446-3847)** · Email **[heath.shepard@kw.com](mailto:heath.shepard@kw.com)**

---

*This is not investment, legal or tax advice. Talk with a CPA about depreciation, rollback taxes, the circuit breaker and 1031 timing, a lender about financing structure, Kendall Appraisal District about valuation and exemptions, and the City of Boerne Planning Department about short-term rental eligibility for a specific address.*

question: Is Boerne, Texas good for short-term rentals?
metaTitle: Is Boerne, Texas good for short-term rentals?
metaDescription: What caps a Boerne STR: a 200-foot block-face rule, two per bedroom plus two, no events, 13 percent hotel tax, and $500,000 liability coverage.
shortAnswer: Boerne allows short-term rentals under Ordinance No. 2023-09, so the real question is what caps the return. The binding constraints are a 200-foot block-face separation in residential zones, occupancy of two per bedroom plus two, a ban on events, 13 percent hotel occupancy tax, and a $500,000 liability insurance minimum.
body:
## The regulatory picture in one screen

Boerne is not a prohibition city and it is not an open city. It licenses. The full mechanics live on a separate page — [what are the short-term rental rules in Boerne](/boerne/boerne-tx-short-term-rental-rules) — but the parts that shape an underwriting model are these, all from the [City of Boerne's short-term rental page](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/2444/Short-Term-Rentals):

- **$200 registration, two-year permit term**, $200 renewal filed within 30 days of expiration.
- **Safety inspection** required inside the city limits, $100 through a city inspector or done by an outside licensed inspector. Not required in the ETJ.
- **Liability insurance: $500,000 per occurrence and $1,000,000 aggregate.**
- **200-foot separation from another STR on the same block face** in residentially zoned areas.
- **Occupancy: two people per bedroom plus two additional people.** One parking space per bedroom.
- **Events prohibited.**
- **Hotel occupancy tax** remitted through the city portal.
- Rules reach the **city limits and the ETJ**.

One more thing before the analysis: **Boerne is the county seat of Kendall County, not part of the City of San Antonio and not in Bexar County.** San Antonio's STR ordinance, with its own permit types and density formula, does not apply here. Investors read the San Antonio rules constantly and then buy in Boerne. Different rulebook.

## The permit is two years, and what happens on resale is a question for the city

The ordinance sets a two-year term. The posted materials do not resolve whether an existing permit transfers to a new owner when the property sells. Treat that as unanswered until the **Boerne Planning Department** answers it in writing for the specific address.

That is not a technicality. If a permit does not run with the property, a buyer paying an STR price is buying income that depends on an approval they do not yet hold. And if the block-face situation has changed since the seller's permit was issued, a fresh application may not be grantable at all.

## The block-face rule caps supply exactly where demand is

In residentially zoned areas, an STR cannot operate within **200 feet of another STR on the same block face**, including residentially zoned property inside the Historic, Downtown and River Road overlay districts ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/CivicAlerts.aspx?AID=1437&ARC=2987)). In the commercial portions of those overlays there is no separation requirement. Outside those overlays, STRs are prohibited in commercial zones.

The practical effect is the single most important fact on this page. The blocks closest to the Hill Country Mile — the walkable ones where a guest will pay a premium to park once and stay put — are exactly the blocks where the 200-foot allowance is most likely to already be consumed by an existing permit holder. A property can be a perfect STR in every respect and still be ineligible because a neighbor filed first.

This cuts both ways for an owner who clears it. Supply on a given block face is limited by ordinance, not by market appetite. That is a durable moat for a permit that already exists — and a hard wall for one that does not.

**Confirm eligibility for the exact address with the Planning Department at (830) 248-1501 during the option period**, not after closing.

## Occupancy sets a hard ceiling on the revenue model

Two per bedroom plus two. A two-bedroom sleeps six. A three-bedroom sleeps eight. A four-bedroom sleeps ten.

That ceiling is what makes the large-group play difficult in Boerne's residential zones. A five-bedroom ranch house marketed to a reunion of eighteen cannot legally host eighteen, and a listing advertising that headcount is advertising a violation. If the model depends on a per-head rate times a large party, the ordinance has already priced it out.

Parking is one space per bedroom, with street parking allowed — which matters on the narrow older streets near downtown where on-site parking is scarce and neighbor complaints start.

## Events are prohibited, so the venue play is off the table

Occupants may not hold events at the property. No weddings, no receptions, no corporate offsites, no paid photo shoots dressed up as a stay.

This closes a specific arbitrage that works in other Hill Country markets: buy acreage, rent it nightly, and sell the venue separately at a multiple of the nightly rate. In Boerne's STR framework that second revenue line does not exist. Anyone underwriting a Boerne property on event income is underwriting income the ordinance does not allow.

## Tax and insurance are real line items, not rounding

**Hotel occupancy tax in Boerne runs 13 percent combined — 6 percent state and 7 percent city** ([City of Boerne, Current Tax Rates](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/646/Current-Tax-Rates)), remitted through the city portal. Whether a booking platform collects and remits any portion on a host's behalf is a question for the platform and for a **CPA**; the obligation sits with the operator either way.

The insurance minimum — **$500,000 per occurrence and $1,000,000 aggregate** — is the item most often missed at the modeling stage. A standard HO-3 homeowner's policy generally excludes commercial or transient-occupancy use, so the premium in the spreadsheet is usually the wrong premium. Get a real quote from an **insurance agent who writes short-term rental coverage** before the offer, not a placeholder.

Property tax is its own adjustment. A short-term rental is not a residence homestead, so it gets no homestead exemption and no 10 percent homestead cap. See [how rental properties are taxed differently in Texas](/answers/how-are-rental-properties-taxed-differently-in-texas).

## The demand side, stated only as far as the data goes

What is verifiable: **Kendall County grew 20.3 percent between 2020 and 2025**, from an estimated 44,568 to 53,289, with most of that coming from domestic migration — people moving in ([Community Impact](https://communityimpact.com/san-antonio/boerne-fair-oaks-ranch/government/2026/03/30/kendall-county-population-increases-by-203-from-2020-2025/)). Boerne is the Hill Country county seat roughly **31 miles from San Antonio on Interstate 10**, which puts a metro of that size inside an easy drive for a weekend stay.

That is a real demand story. It is not an occupancy rate, an average daily rate, a RevPAR figure or a cap rate, and nobody should accept those numbers from a blog post about a market this small. Submarket performance in Boerne varies block to block — largely because of the block-face rule above.

## What to actually do before writing an offer

1. **Confirm STR eligibility for the specific address** with the City of Boerne Planning Department, and get the answer on permit transferability in writing.
2. **Check the deed restrictions and any POA declaration.** A city permit is not HOA permission. See [can an HOA ban short-term rentals in Texas](/answers/can-an-hoa-ban-short-term-rentals-in-texas).
3. **Pull actual comparable performance data** for real Boerne listings at a similar bedroom count and location, rather than a market-level average.
4. **Have a CPA model it** with hotel occupancy tax, the non-homestead property tax treatment, the real insurance quote, cleaning and management, and the reserve for a two-year permit cycle.
5. Build the analysis so it still works if the permit needs to be applied for fresh.

Boerne can work as a short-term rental market. Whether a particular house works is a question about that block face, that declaration, and that pro forma — and all three are answerable before the option period ends.

question: Is Boerne, Texas a good place to live?
metaTitle: Is Boerne, Texas a good place to live?
metaDescription: Boerne trades a 31-mile I-10 commute and annual reappraisal for A-rated schools and Hill Country land, with Kendall County up 20.3 percent since 2020.
shortAnswer: Boerne works well if you want Hill Country land, an A-rated school district, and a 30-to-45-minute I-10 commute to San Antonio. It is the county seat of Kendall County, not a San Antonio suburb. The trade-offs are 20.3 percent county growth since 2020, groundwater limits, and annual market-value reappraisal.
body:
## Start with the jurisdiction, because it drives everything else

Boerne is the **county seat of Kendall County**, about **31 miles northwest of San Antonio on Interstate 10** ([City-Data, Boerne](https://www.city-data.com/city/Boerne-Texas.html)). ZIP codes are 78006 and 78015.

That sentence decides more than it looks like it does. Boerne is not in Bexar County and it is not inside the City of San Antonio. San Antonio's ordinances — short-term rental rules, tree ordinances, permitting — have no force here. Your appraisal district is **Kendall Appraisal District** at [kendallad.org](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/), not Bexar CAD, and that is where a homestead exemption and a protest get filed. People relocating from inside Loop 1604 routinely file with the wrong district the first year and lose the exemption for that tax year.

## The schools are the single strongest argument

**Boerne ISD earned an "A" rating from the Texas Education Agency for six consecutive years**, including the 2024 and 2025 rating years, and scored **92 points** in the 2024–2025 ratings with **20 distinction designations** ([Boerne Star](https://www.boernestar.com/article/11432,boerne-isd-six-straight-years-of-a-ratings); [TEA 2025 accountability](https://tea.texas.gov/texas-schools/accountability/academic-accountability/performance-reporting/2025-accountability-rating-system)).

District-wide is not campus-by-campus. The Boerne Star reported that **Viola Wilson, Currington, Herff and Kendall elementaries received lower grades** in the same rating cycle. If you are buying for a specific elementary attendance zone, look up that campus, not the district average, and confirm the current zone with the district — attendance boundaries in a fast-growing district move.

## Commute reality

Downtown San Antonio is a **30-to-45-minute drive depending on traffic**. The I-10 corridor between Boerne and Loop 1604 is the pinch point, and it does not behave the same at 7:15 a.m. as it does at 10 a.m. Drive it, on a weekday, at the hour you would actually drive it, before you decide a neighborhood works.

Boerne is also a place people work rather than only sleep. It is the county seat, so county offices are here, and the city runs its own utilities. That matters less for commute math than for the fact that the town does not empty out at 8 a.m.

## Growth is the real change

**Kendall County grew 20.3 percent between 2020 and 2025**, from an estimated **44,568 to 53,289 residents**, and most of that was **domestic migration** — people moving in from elsewhere in the United States ([Community Impact](https://communityimpact.com/san-antonio/boerne-fair-oaks-ranch/government/2026/03/30/kendall-county-population-increases-by-203-from-2020-2025/)).

The **City of Boerne's 2020 census population was 18,084**, and 2026 figures are estimates that vary by source — World Population Review estimates roughly 25,209 ([World Population Review](https://worldpopulationreview.com/us-cities/texas/boerne)). Treat those as estimates, not counts.

What that growth feels like on the ground: more traffic on Main and on I-10, school capacity planning, and new subdivisions where there was ranch land. Whether that is a reason to buy now or a reason to buy farther out is a personal call, but it is not a rumor. It is in the census estimates.

## The tax trade-off nobody explains before the first bill

Texas has no state individual income tax. Texas funds local government primarily through property tax instead, and Texas property is **reappraised at market value annually**, subject to a **10 percent homestead cap** on net appraised value once a homestead exemption is in place ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)).

For a home inside the city limits in Boerne ISD, the 2025 adopted rates per $100 of taxable value were:

- **Boerne ISD: 1.0109** — 0.6969 maintenance and operations plus 0.3140 debt ([Kendall County](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/295/Boerne-ISD)).
- **City of Boerne: 0.4716** ([Kendall County](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/297/Boerne-City-of)).
- **Kendall County: 0.377** — 0.317976 M&O plus 0.059024 debt, down from 0.3827 in 2024 ([Kendall County](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/306/Kendall-County)).

Any special district on the parcel adds to that. Sales tax in Boerne is **8.25 percent total**: 6.25 percent state, 1.50 percent city, 0.50 percent county ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/646/Current-Tax-Rates)).

Buyers coming from California hit this hardest, because Proposition 13 limits reassessment there and Texas does not work that way. A **CPA or tax advisor** is the right person to model your own before-and-after.

## Water is a live constraint, not a talking point

Boerne's drinking water comes from three sources: **Canyon Lake surface water purchased through the Guadalupe-Blanco River Authority, Boerne City Lake, and local wells in the Trinity Group aquifers** ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/FAQ.aspx?QID=315)).

Groundwater in Kendall County is regulated by the **Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District**, which sets drought stages using roughly 42 monitor wells, stream gauges on Cibolo Creek and the Guadalupe River, and more than 100 rain gauge sites ([Cow Creek GCD](https://ccgcd.org/)). Stages move. Check [ccgcd.org](https://ccgcd.org/) for the current one rather than trusting a number in any article, including this one.

If you are buying acreage on a well instead of a city tap, that is a different due-diligence problem. Well yield, depth, casing condition and the district's rules on permitted pumping all belong in your inspection window.

## Who Boerne is not for

Someone who wants a five-minute commute to the Medical Center. Someone who needs walkable everything — Boerne has a genuinely walkable downtown, but the rest is car country. Someone who wants a low tax bill in absolute dollars; Boerne ISD's rate plus a Hill Country valuation adds up. And someone buying acreage expecting no rules, because groundwater regulation, deed restrictions and the city's extraterritorial jurisdiction all reach past the city limit sign.

question: Is Boerne, Texas growing?
metaTitle: Is Boerne, Texas growing?
metaDescription: Kendall County went from 44,568 residents in 2020 to 53,289 in 2025, up 20.3 percent on domestic migration. Boerne's 2020 census count was 18,084.
shortAnswer: Yes. Kendall County grew 20.3 percent between 2020 and 2025, from an estimated 44,568 residents to 53,289, and most of that came from domestic migration rather than births. The City of Boerne's 2020 census population was 18,084; current city-level numbers are estimates that vary by source.
body:
## The county number is the reliable one

**Kendall County: 44,568 in 2020, 53,289 in 2025 — up 20.3 percent** ([Community Impact](https://communityimpact.com/san-antonio/boerne-fair-oaks-ranch/government/2026/03/30/kendall-county-population-increases-by-203-from-2020-2025/)). Boerne is the **county seat of Kendall County**, roughly 31 miles northwest of San Antonio on I-10 ([City-Data](https://www.city-data.com/city/Boerne-Texas.html)).

County-level estimates are the number to quote, because they are produced on a consistent methodology and they capture the unincorporated acreage where a lot of the actual growth is landing. City limits are a political boundary; growth does not respect it.

## The city number needs a caveat

The **2020 decennial census counted 18,084 people in the City of Boerne**. Estimates for 2026 vary by source — World Population Review puts it around 25,209, and other projections land lower ([World Population Review](https://worldpopulationreview.com/us-cities/texas/boerne)).

Use the 2020 census figure as the hard number and describe anything after it as an estimate. Different vendors use different base years, different annexation assumptions and different household-size models, which is why a "Boerne population" search returns four different answers.

## "Domestic migration" is the important word

Most of Kendall County's growth is people moving in from elsewhere in the United States, not natural increase ([Community Impact](https://communityimpact.com/san-antonio/boerne-fair-oaks-ranch/government/2026/03/30/kendall-county-population-increases-by-203-from-2020-2025/)).

That distinction changes what the growth does to the market. Natural increase adds people slowly and adds households later, when those children form their own. In-migration adds a household on day one, usually with proceeds from a previous sale, and usually with an opinion about price formed somewhere more expensive. It is the fastest-acting kind of demand there is.

## Where the growth actually goes

Three places, and they are governed differently:

1. **Inside Boerne city limits** — city utilities, city ordinances, city tax rate, platting through the City of Boerne.
2. **Boerne's extraterritorial jurisdiction (ETJ)** — unincorporated, but the city retains regulatory authority over subdivision platting under Texas Local Government Code Chapter 42, and some city ordinances explicitly reach the ETJ.
3. **Unincorporated Kendall County outside the ETJ** — no city tax rate, no city services, well and septic, and a much narrower set of local rules.

A buyer comparing two listings five miles apart can be comparing two different regulatory worlds. Confirm which one a specific address sits in with the **City of Boerne Planning Department** before assuming anything about utilities, permitting or what can be built next door.

## What growth is pressing against

**Schools.** Boerne ISD has held an **"A" rating from the Texas Education Agency for six consecutive years** ([Boerne Star](https://www.boernestar.com/article/11432,boerne-isd-six-straight-years-of-a-ratings)). Sustaining that through enrollment growth is a capacity and staffing problem, and it is why the district's rate carries a debt component — **1.0109 total for 2025, of which 0.3140 is debt service** ([Kendall County](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/295/Boerne-ISD)). School bonds are how fast-growing districts build classrooms, and they land on the tax bill.

**Water.** The city draws from three sources: **Canyon Lake surface water through the Guadalupe-Blanco River Authority, Boerne City Lake, and local Trinity Group aquifer wells** ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/FAQ.aspx?QID=315)). Groundwater is regulated countywide by the **Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District** ([ccgcd.org](https://ccgcd.org/)). More rooftops on a fixed aquifer is the constraint that shapes how much of this growth can continue and where.

**Roads.** I-10 is the single artery. Everything that grows here commutes on it.

## Context: the neighbors are growing too

Boerne is not growing in isolation. **Fair Oaks Ranch** incorporated in **1988** and had a **2020 census population of 9,833**, with city limits spanning **Bexar, Comal and Kendall counties** ([Wikipedia, Fair Oaks Ranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_Oaks_Ranch,_Texas)). **Bulverde**, in **Comal County**, incorporated in **1999** and counted **5,692** in 2020 ([Wikipedia, Bulverde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulverde,_Texas)). The whole northwest arc out of San Antonio is absorbing the same in-migration; Boerne is simply the largest and oldest town in it.

## What this means if you are buying

Three practical consequences:

- **Inventory turns over faster than a small-town reputation suggests.** A well-priced house in a good attendance zone does not sit.
- **New construction competes with resale.** In a growth market the builder down the road is a comparable sale, and builder incentives move the resale ceiling.
- **Today's edge-of-town lot is tomorrow's interior lot.** That is good for value and bad for the view. Ask what is zoned, platted or filed for development on the adjacent tracts — the Planning Department, not the seller, is the source for that.

## Related questions

- [Why are homes in Boerne, Texas so expensive?](/answers/why-are-homes-in-boerne-so-expensive)
- [Does Boerne have enough water?](/answers/does-boerne-have-enough-water)

question: Is Texas Hill Country land a good investment?
metaTitle: Is Texas Hill Country land a good investment?
metaDescription: Ag valuation under 1-d-1, the three-year rollback under Tax Code 23.55, Cow Creek groundwater rules and legal access decide a Hill Country tract.
shortAnswer: Hill Country land is not a passive investment. The numbers that decide it are specific to the tract: whether it carries 1-d-1 open-space ag valuation, what a change of use would trigger in rollback taxes for the prior three years, legal access and easements, groundwater availability under Cow Creek GCD rules, and septic feasibility.
body:
Land is sold on scenery and bought on diligence. A tract with a view and a low price per acre can carry a tax status that collapses the year you change what you do with it, a well that will not produce, an access easement that is not recorded, and no realistic path to a septic permit. None of that shows up in the listing. All of it shows up in the closing file or the year after.

## Ag valuation is the biggest single line item, and it is conditional

Most rural Texas tracts are taxed not on market value but on **productivity value** under **1-d-1 open-space appraisal**. That is a large reduction, and it is the reason a 40-acre tract can carry a smaller tax bill than a house in town.

It is also conditional. Under the [Texas Comptroller's ag and timber rules](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/ag-timber/index.php), 1-d-1 open-space appraisal requires:

- **current principal agricultural use** of the land;
- use to the **degree of intensity generally accepted in the area** — a local standard the appraisal district applies, not a number you choose; and
- **agricultural or timber production in 5 of the preceding 7 years**.

"Degree of intensity generally accepted in the area" is the phrase to underline. It means a few animals on a large tract may not qualify. What counts is set locally, and in Kendall County the people who decide it are at **[Kendall Appraisal District](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)** — not Bexar CAD, because Boerne and Kendall County are not in Bexar County or the City of San Antonio.

**Wildlife management use** is the alternative that suits buyers who are not going to run cattle. The land must have been **previously qualified** as open-space or timber land, and it must be used in **at least 3 of 7** specified ways to propagate a sustaining breeding, migrating or wintering population of indigenous wild animals. The word "previously qualified" is the gate: wildlife management is a conversion of an existing ag valuation, not a fresh start on land that never had one.

Before writing an offer, ask the appraisal district what the tract currently carries, what the qualifying use is, and what it would take to keep it.

## The rollback tax is the thing that surprises buyers

Take ag-valued land out of ag use and the appraisal district assesses an **additional tax** — the rollback. Under **Texas Tax Code §23.55**, it equals "the difference between the taxes imposed on the land for each of the **three years preceding** the year in which the change of use occurs" ([Texas Tax Code §23.55](https://codes.findlaw.com/tx/tax-code/tax-sect-23-55/)) — the gap between what was paid on productivity value and what would have been paid on market value.

Two corrections worth making, because both circulate widely.

**First: the buyer who changes the use inherits the bill.** The rollback is triggered by the change of use, not by the sale. A buyer who closes on an ag-valued tract, stops running livestock, and puts up a house is the one holding the assessment, for tax years in which the seller owned the land and got the benefit. Nobody is required to warn you.

**Second: there is no separate statutory rollback interest rate.** A great many land-buying articles publish a 5% or 7% "rollback interest" figure. §23.55 does not impose one. It provides only that the additional taxes incur "penalties and interest as provided by law for ad valorem taxes imposed by the taxing unit" if they are not paid by the delinquency deadline. That is ordinary delinquency interest on an unpaid bill, not a rollback surcharge. Treat any page quoting a specific rollback interest percentage as unsourced.

What the rollback actually costs on a given tract is arithmetic on that tract's own three-year history and the rates of every entity that taxes it. Kendall County parcels sit under a stack that can include Boerne ISD or Comfort ISD, the City of Boerne, Kendall County, Kendall County MUD, Miralomas MUD, the Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District, and Kendall County WCID #1 ([Kendall AD](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/); [Kendall County tax rate information](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/184/Tax-Rate-Information)). Get the number from the appraisal district before you commit, and take the consequences to a CPA.

## Water is a permitting question, not a plumbing question

Groundwater in Kendall County is regulated by the **[Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District](https://ccgcd.org/)**, which sets drought stages using data from roughly 42 monitor wells, stream gauges on Cibolo Creek and the Guadalupe River, and more than 100 rain gauge sites. Cow Creek is also a taxing entity on Kendall County bills.

Drought stages move, and stage rules can restrict permitted pumping. Do not take a stage from any article, including this one. Check the district for the current stage and for what it means for a new or existing well on the tract.

The questions to ask before buying land you intend to build on:

- Is there an existing well, and what does it actually produce today — not what the seller remembers it producing?
- What does Cow Creek require to permit a new well on this tract, and are there spacing or production conditions?
- Do the water rights convey? TREC publishes a **Seller's Disclosure about Groundwater and Surface Water Rights, form 61-0, effective 07/01/2026** ([TREC](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/contracts)), which exists precisely because buyers assume water rights follow the dirt.

A tract with no viable water is not cheap land. It is a different asset.

## Access, easements and the rest of the diligence list

Each of these is a separate item with a separate professional attached, and each one has sunk a Hill Country land deal:

- **Legal access.** Does the tract have recorded, deeded access to a public road, or does the driveway cross a neighbor's land on a handshake? An easement that is not recorded is not access. This is a title and survey question and a **Texas real estate attorney** question.
- **Survey.** Acreage, boundaries, encroachments, the location of easements and any floodplain line. On raw land this is not optional.
- **Utilities.** Distance to the nearest electric service and the cost to extend it. That number can be large and it is quoted by the utility, not estimated by anyone else.
- **Septic feasibility.** Hill Country soil over limestone is thin. Whether a conventional system will perc, or whether the tract needs an engineered aerobic system, changes the build budget materially. That is a soil evaluation, done before closing, not after.
- **Minerals.** Texas allows severed mineral estates, and a prior owner may have reserved them. TREC has an **Addendum for Reservation of Oil, Gas, and Other Minerals, form 44-3, effective 02/01/2023**.
- **Deed restrictions and any POA.** Private restrictions can control building size, materials, livestock, subdivision and short-term rental use, and they are enforceable regardless of what zoning says.
- **Which contract form applies.** Vacant land generally uses the **Unimproved Property Contract, TREC form 9-18, effective 07/01/2026**; a tract with a home and acreage generally uses the **Farm and Ranch Contract, form 25-17, effective 07/01/2026** ([TREC](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/contracts)).

## Financing raw land is its own product

Raw land does not finance like a house. Terms, down payment and amortization are different, and the lenders who do it are often not the lenders who do residential mortgages. A buyer planning to build should get the land loan and the construction financing structured together with a **lender** before writing an offer, not after. Nothing about raw land financing should be assumed from residential experience.

## The demand side, stated honestly

**Kendall County grew 20.3% between 2020 and 2025**, from an estimated 44,568 to 53,289, driven mostly by domestic migration ([Community Impact](https://communityimpact.com/san-antonio/boerne-fair-oaks-ranch/government/2026/03/30/kendall-county-population-increases-by-203-from-2020-2025/)).

That is a real, sourced population trend, and it is the strongest available argument that demand for land here is not hypothetical. It is not a forecast, and it is not a return.

**This page does not publish land prices per acre, appreciation rates or absorption figures.** Those vary enormously by location, access, water, topography and tract size, they move constantly, and a number pulled off a blog is worse than no number. Ask for current comparable land sales, dated, for the specific area and tract size you are considering.

## The honest summary

Hill Country land can be a good investment. It is never an easy one. The tracts that work are the ones where a buyer priced the ag status, the rollback exposure, the water, the access and the septic before closing instead of discovering them afterward. The tracts that go wrong almost always go wrong on one of those five.

## Who answers which question

- **Kendall Appraisal District** — current ag valuation status, qualifying use, degree of intensity, and what a rollback would be on this tract.
- **A CPA or tax advisor** — the tax consequences of a change of use, and how the rollback lands on your return.
- **A Texas real estate attorney** — access, easements, deed restrictions, severed minerals, title defects.
- **Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District** — well permitting and current drought stage.
- **A surveyor, a licensed inspector and a septic professional** — boundaries, improvements and system feasibility.
- **A lender** — land loan structure and construction financing.

## Related questions

- [What is an ag exemption in Texas, and what are rollback taxes?](/answers/what-is-an-ag-exemption-in-texas-and-what-are-rollback-taxes)
- [What should I know about septic and wells in the Hill Country?](/answers/what-should-i-know-about-septic-and-wells-in-the-hill-country)
- [Does Boerne have enough water?](/answers/does-boerne-have-enough-water)
- [Is Boerne, Texas growing?](/answers/is-boerne-texas-growing)
- [Is Boerne a good real estate investment?](/answers/is-boerne-a-good-real-estate-investment)

question: Is the option fee refundable in Texas?
metaTitle: Is the option fee refundable in Texas?
metaDescription: Is the Texas option fee refundable? No — but it is credited to the sales price at closing. Here is the difference between the option fee and earnest money.
shortAnswer: No. The option fee is not refundable. If the buyer terminates during the option period, the seller keeps it — that is what the fee bought. If the sale closes, the fee is credited to the sales price, so the buyer effectively gets it back at the closing table. Earnest money is the refundable deposit.
body:
## Why it is not refundable

The option fee is consideration for a right, not a deposit. The buyer is purchasing an **unrestricted right to terminate** the contract during the option period, for any reason or no reason at all. The seller sells that right and gets paid for it.

The contract says so in terms. Paragraph 5B of TREC form 20-19 provides that if the buyer gives notice of termination within the time prescribed, "(i) **the option fee will not be refunded** and Escrow Agent shall release any option fee remaining with Escrow Agent to Seller; and (ii) **any earnest money will be refunded to Buyer**" ([TREC form 20-19, ¶5B](https://www.trec.texas.gov/sites/default/files/pdf-forms/20-19_4.pdf)).

That single sentence is the whole answer. The fee goes to the seller. The earnest money comes back.

Refunding the fee would mean the buyer got the right for free. That is not the bargain, and it is not how the contract is written. The seller earns the fee by taking the property off the market and accepting that the buyer can walk with no justification required. Whether the buyer uses the right or not, the seller provided it.

## The question most people are actually asking

Almost nobody asks "is the option fee refundable" because they want a vocabulary lesson. They are asking one of two things.

**"If I back out, do I lose money?"** Yes — you lose the option fee. Your earnest money comes back to you, assuming you terminated properly and on time.

**"If I buy the house, did I pay that for nothing?"** No. Paragraph 5A(4) of the contract: "**The option fee will be credited to the Sales Price at closing**" ([TREC form 20-19, ¶5A(4)](https://www.trec.texas.gov/sites/default/files/pdf-forms/20-19_4.pdf)). It shows on the buyer's side of the settlement statement as a credit and reduces the cash needed at the table by that amount. You do not pay it twice.

So "not refundable" and "you get it back" are both true, in different scenarios. Non-refundable on termination. Credited on closing.

## Option fee versus earnest money

These are two different amounts with two different jobs, and they behave nothing alike.

| | Option fee | Earnest money |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | Payment for the right to terminate | Good-faith deposit toward the purchase |
| Whose money once delivered | The seller's | Still the buyer's, held in escrow |
| Refundable on option-period termination | No | Yes |
| At closing | Credited to the sales price | Credited to the buyer |
| Can be released early | Yes — escrow may pay it to the seller before closing without the buyer's consent | No — requires mutual agreement or a court order |

That last row is the one that surprises people, and the buyer signed up for it. Paragraph 5A(4): "Buyer authorizes Escrow Agent to release and deliver the option fee to Seller **at any time without further notice to or consent from Buyer**, and releases Escrow Agent from liability for delivery of the option fee to Seller" ([TREC form 20-19, ¶5A(4)](https://www.trec.texas.gov/sites/default/files/pdf-forms/20-19_4.pdf)). Earnest money cannot move that way. It sits in escrow until both sides sign a release or a court orders it.

## Is there any situation where the fee comes back?

Not through the option mechanism. The fee is non-refundable by design, and there is no statutory right to claw it back.

Two things get confused with a refund:

**The credit at closing.** Covered above. That is not a refund, it is a credit against the price.

**A negotiated return.** Buyer and seller can agree to anything they both sign. If a seller wants to return the option fee as part of settling a dispute, or as a concession in a re-negotiation, nothing prevents it. That is a deal term the parties write, not a right the buyer has. A Texas real estate attorney is the right person to look at any agreement that moves money after a termination.

## The failure that actually costs buyers money

The bigger risk is not losing the option fee. It is losing the *right* the option fee paid for.

Paragraph 5D spells out both ways that happens:

> "If **no dollar amount is stated** as the option fee or if Buyer fails to deliver the option fee within the time required, **Buyer shall not have the unrestricted right to terminate** this contract under this paragraph 5."

([TREC form 20-19, ¶5D](https://www.trec.texas.gov/sites/default/files/pdf-forms/20-19_4.pdf))

**Late delivery.** Paragraph 5A requires the fee to reach the escrow agent within 3 days after the effective date. Paragraph 5A(2) extends that only if the last day is a Saturday, Sunday or Legal Holiday, as defined by Texas Government Code Sections 662.003(a) and 662.003(b)(4) and (6). Paragraph 5E: "**Time is of the essence** for this paragraph and strict compliance with the time for performance is required."

**A blank option fee.** This one has nothing to do with timing. A contract with an option period filled in and the option fee dollar blank left empty gives the buyer no unrestricted right to terminate at all. Nobody misses a deadline; the right simply never existed. Read your own executed ¶5A and confirm there is a dollar figure in it.

Either way the buyer is in a contract they cannot freely exit, with earnest money exposed.

The combined payment adds a third exposure. Paragraph 5A allows the option fee and earnest money to be paid separately or combined, and ¶5A(3) applies amounts received "first to the option fee, then to the earnest money, and then to the additional earnest money." A combined payment that is short by any amount fully funds the option fee and leaves the earnest money underfunded — which is a buyer default, not a clerical issue.

## Terminating the right way

Paragraph 5B requires notice of termination to the seller, and specifies that "Notices under this paragraph must be given **by 5:00 p.m. (local time where the Property is located)** by the date specified" ([TREC form 20-19, ¶5B](https://www.trec.texas.gov/sites/default/files/pdf-forms/20-19_4.pdf)). TREC publishes a form for it: **Notice of Buyer's Termination of Contract, form 38-8, effective 04/01/2025** ([TREC contract forms](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/contracts)).

Do that, and the seller keeps the option fee and the earnest money goes back to the buyer. Miss the 5:00 p.m. deadline and the buyer has paid for a right that expired unused.

## Related questions

- [How does the option fee work in Texas?](/answers/how-does-the-option-fee-work-in-texas)
- [What is the option period in a Texas real estate contract?](/answers/what-is-the-option-period-in-texas)
- [What is earnest money in Texas, and is it refundable?](/answers/what-is-earnest-money-in-texas-and-is-it-refundable)
- [How do I terminate a real estate contract in Texas?](/answers/how-do-i-terminate-a-contract-in-texas)
