question: What should I know about moving from Austin to Boerne?
metaTitle: What should I know about moving from Austin to Boerne?
metaDescription: Leaving Travis County means Kendall Appraisal District, Boerne ISD, a 1.8595 combined tax rate before exemptions, and a different water picture.
shortAnswer: Boerne is in Kendall County, not Travis County: a different appraisal district (Kendall Appraisal District), a different school district (Boerne ISD), and a different water picture. It sits about 31 miles northwest of San Antonio on Interstate 10, a 30 to 45 minute drive downtown depending on traffic.
body:
## Everything administrative changes

An Austin-to-Boerne move is not a move across town. It is a move into a different county, which means a different set of institutions handles everything you have gotten used to.

**Appraisal district.** Boerne property is appraised by **[Kendall Appraisal District](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)**, not Travis CAD. That is where the homestead exemption is filed, where the appraisal notice comes from, and where a protest is heard. A homestead exemption does not follow you from a Travis County property. It is filed fresh, on the new address, with the new district.

**School district.** Boerne is served by **Boerne ISD**, and part of the county is served by **Comfort ISD**. Neither is an Austin-area district and neither shares Austin-area boundaries, calendars or bond history.

**City.** Boerne is the county seat of Kendall County. It is not in the City of San Antonio and not in Bexar County — San Antonio ordinances do not apply here, which matters if you are researching anything on a San Antonio city page and assuming it carries over. The City of Boerne is at 201 East San Antonio Avenue, Boerne, TX 78006, 830-249-9343. ZIP codes are 78006 and 78015.

## The tax bill is built differently, and you have to read the entity list

A Kendall County property tax bill stacks every taxing entity whose boundary touches the parcel. The entities that appear on Kendall County bills include Boerne ISD, Comfort ISD, the City of Boerne, Kendall County, Kendall County MUD, Miralomas MUD, the Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District, and Kendall County WCID #1 ([Kendall AD](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)).

For a home inside the Boerne city limits, in Boerne ISD, the 2025 stack was, per $100 of taxable value:

| Entity | 2025 rate |
|---|---|
| Boerne ISD | **1.0109** (M&O 0.6969 + debt 0.3140, up from 0.9909 in 2024) |
| City of Boerne | **0.4716** (unchanged from 2024) |
| Kendall County | **0.377** (M&O 0.317976 + debt 0.059024) |
| **Combined** | **1.8595** |

Sources: [Boerne ISD rates](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/295/Boerne-ISD), [City of Boerne rates](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/297/Boerne-City-of), [Kendall County rates](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/306/Kendall-County).

That combined figure is **before any special district on the parcel and before exemptions**. Part of the county is in **Comfort ISD**, whose 2025 rate was **0.9328** ([Kendall County](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/300/Kendall-County)). Kendall County's **2026 adopted rate is 0.373**, continuing a downward drift from 0.3827 in 2024 and 0.412700 in 2021 — which does not mean a falling bill, because values are reappraised annually.

Rates change each fall. Pull the current set from [Kendall County Tax Rate Information](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/184/Tax-Rate-Information) before you build a payment estimate on them, and pull the entity list for your specific parcel from [Kendall AD](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/).

The line worth checking on any specific address is the MUD or WCID line. A newer subdivision can carry a district rate that an older in-town property does not, and it will not show up in a generic "Boerne tax rate" number.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD earned an "A" rating from the Texas Education Agency for six consecutive years**, including the 2024 and 2025 rating years, and scored **92 points** in the 2024-2025 ratings with **20 distinction designations** ([Boerne Star](https://www.boernestar.com/article/11432,boerne-isd-six-straight-years-of-a-ratings); [TEA](https://tea.texas.gov/texas-schools/accountability/academic-accountability/performance-reporting/2025-accountability-rating-system)).

Not every campus rated A. The Boerne Star reported that Viola Wilson, Currington, Herff and Kendall elementaries received lower grades. A parent moving from an Austin-area district should look at the specific campus that serves the specific address rather than the district-level letter, because attendance zones in a growing district move.

## The orientation flips toward San Antonio

Boerne runs on **Interstate 10** and faces San Antonio, roughly **31 miles southeast**, a **30 to 45 minute** drive to downtown San Antonio depending on traffic ([city-data](https://www.city-data.com/city/Boerne-Texas.html)).

That is the practical reorientation of the move. Medical centers, the airport, professional services and most big-ticket shopping are a San Antonio trip, not an Austin trip. Anyone who needs to be in Austin regularly should drive the route at the hour they would actually drive it, on a weekday, before committing — that is a real number you should measure yourself rather than take from any page.

## Water is the structural difference, and it deserves an hour of your time

This is the part Austin transplants underestimate.

Boerne's drinking water comes from three sources: **Canyon Lake surface water purchased through the Guadalupe-Blanco River Authority**, **Boerne City Lake**, and **local wells in the Trinity Group aquifers** ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/FAQ.aspx?QID=315)). That is a genuinely different supply structure from a large municipal system, and it is diversified precisely because no single source is abundant.

Groundwater in Kendall County is regulated by the **[Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District](https://ccgcd.org/)**, which sets drought stages using data from roughly 42 monitor wells, stream gauges on Cibolo Creek and the Guadalupe River, and more than 100 rain gauge sites. Cow Creek is also a taxing entity on Kendall County bills.

Drought stages move. Do not take a stage from any article, including this one — check [ccgcd.org](https://ccgcd.org/) for the current stage and the restrictions attached to it before you plan a lawn, a pool or livestock.

Two address-specific questions follow from this and both belong in the option period:

1. **Is this property on city water or on a well?** Outside the city limits, many are on wells, and a well is a private water system you own and maintain.
2. **Is it on sewer or on septic?** Outside the city, septic is common. Septic condition, capacity and permitting are inspection items, and a failing system is expensive.

## The county is growing fast

**Kendall County grew 20.3% between 2020 and 2025**, from an estimated 44,568 to 53,289, driven mostly by domestic migration ([Community Impact](https://communityimpact.com/san-antonio/boerne-fair-oaks-ranch/government/2026/03/30/kendall-county-population-increases-by-203-from-2020-2025/)).

Growth is why the water conversation is live, why school attendance zones move, and why annual reappraisal shows up as a real number on year-two tax bills.

## What this page deliberately does not tell you

It does not compare median home prices between Austin and Boerne. Those figures vary widely by source, by ZIP code and by month, and a stale one is worse than none. Ask for current MLS numbers for the specific neighborhoods you are considering, dated, from an agent who can pull them.

## Who answers which question

- **Kendall Appraisal District** — homestead exemption, appraised value, protest, which districts a parcel sits in.
- **City of Boerne Planning Department** — zoning, permits, ETJ status, short-term rental rules.
- **Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District** — well permitting and current drought stage.
- **A licensed inspector and a septic specialist** — well and septic condition on a specific property.
- **A CPA** — what the move does to your tax picture overall.

## Related questions

- [Is Boerne, Texas a good place to live?](/answers/is-boerne-texas-a-good-place-to-live)
- [Are Boerne ISD schools good?](/answers/are-boerne-isd-schools-good)
- [Does Boerne have enough water?](/answers/does-boerne-have-enough-water)
- [How far is Boerne from San Antonio?](/answers/how-far-is-boerne-from-san-antonio)
- [What are property taxes like in Boerne?](/answers/what-are-property-taxes-like-in-boerne)

## Questions about a specific property?

Call or text **[830-446-3847](tel:+1-830-446-3847)** · Email **[heath.shepard@kw.com](mailto:heath.shepard@kw.com)**

---

*This page describes how Boerne and Kendall County are organized. It is not legal or tax advice. Confirm exemptions and valuations with Kendall Appraisal District, zoning and permits with the City of Boerne Planning Department, and groundwater rules with the Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District.*

question: What should I know about moving from California to the Texas Hill Country?
metaTitle: What should I know about moving from California to the Texas Hill Country?
metaDescription: Moving from California to the Texas Hill Country: the real tax trade, the Boerne and Kendall County entities on a tax bill, and the January 1 homestead rule.
shortAnswer: Texas has no state individual income tax, and it funds local government largely through property tax instead. Texas property is reappraised at market value every year, unlike California under Proposition 13. In Boerne, Boerne ISD's 2025 rate was 1.0109 and the City of Boerne's was 0.4716 per $100 of taxable value.
body:
## The trade you are actually making

California buyers arrive knowing about the income tax. They usually do not arrive knowing that the property tax side works on a completely different principle.

In California, Proposition 13 limits how much a property's assessed value can be reassessed while the same owner holds it. A long-time owner can be paying tax on a number that has very little to do with what the house would sell for today.

Texas does the opposite. Texas appraisal districts value property at **market value, reappraised annually**. Once a homestead exemption is in place there is a **10% per-year cap** on the increase in net appraised value ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)), but that cap limits the speed of the climb, not the destination. Over time, a Texas tax bill tracks the market. A California tax bill, under Prop 13, tracks the purchase.

That is the structural difference, and it is the one that changes a monthly payment five years from now.

Do not let anyone hand you a single "effective rate" comparison between the two states. The honest way to do this is to price your specific Texas address against your specific California situation with a CPA, using the actual rates on the actual parcel.

## Kendall County bills stack several entities

Boerne is the county seat of **Kendall County**. It is not in the City of San Antonio and not in Bexar County, and San Antonio ordinances do not apply here. Your appraisal district is **[Kendall Appraisal District](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)**, not Bexar CAD.

A Texas property tax bill is not one rate. It is the sum of every taxing entity whose boundary covers the parcel. In Kendall County the entities that appear on bills include Boerne ISD, Comfort ISD, the City of Boerne, Kendall County, Kendall County MUD, Miralomas MUD, the Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District, and Kendall County WCID #1 ([Kendall AD](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)).

For a home inside the Boerne city limits, in Boerne ISD, the 2025 stack looked like this, per $100 of taxable value:

| Entity | 2025 rate |
|---|---|
| Boerne ISD | **1.0109** (M&O 0.6969 + debt 0.3140) |
| City of Boerne | **0.4716** |
| Kendall County | **0.377** (M&O 0.317976 + debt 0.059024) |
| **Combined** | **1.8595** |

Sources: [Boerne ISD rates](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/295/Boerne-ISD), [City of Boerne rates](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/297/Boerne-City-of), [Kendall County rates](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/306/Kendall-County).

That combined 1.8595 is **before any special district on the parcel and before any exemption**, and it is not a universal Boerne number. Part of the county is in **Comfort ISD**, whose 2025 rate was **0.9328** ([Kendall County](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/300/Kendall-County)). An address in unincorporated Kendall County does not pay the city rate at all — but it also does not get city services, and it may sit inside a MUD or WCID that adds a line the table above does not show.

The school district is the largest single line on most bills, which is why the school exemption below matters so much.

Rates move every fall with each entity's budget. Boerne ISD was 0.9909 in 2024 and 1.1786 in 2022. The City of Boerne was 0.4766 in 2023. Kendall County has drifted down — 0.3827 in 2024 and 2023, 0.38770 in 2022, 0.412700 in 2021 — and its **2026 adopted rate is 0.373**. A falling rate does not mean a falling bill, because the other half of the equation is the annually reappraised value.

Pull the current set, and the entity list for your specific parcel, from [Kendall County Tax Rate Information](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/184/Tax-Rate-Information) or [Kendall AD's adopted rates page](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/) rather than trusting a number in any article, including this one, as current. MUDs, the WCID and Cow Creek GCD vary parcel by parcel.

## The offsets that bring the number down

Texas gives most of the relief back through homestead exemptions, and they are meaningful.

- **School district residence homestead exemption: $140,000.** Raised from $100,000 by **Proposition 13**, approved by Texas voters in **November 2025** and implemented by **SB 4, 89th Legislature**, effective for tax year 2026 ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)). Yes — Texas's Proposition 13 and California's Proposition 13 are entirely unrelated measures that happen to share a number. Texas's raises an exemption. California's limits reassessment.
- **Local option exemption:** taxing units may offer up to **20%** of appraised value, with a $5,000 minimum.
- **Age 65 or older, or disabled:** school districts must grant an **additional $60,000**, and other taxing units may adopt a local option of at least $3,000. Kendall AD notes that the City of Boerne, Boerne ISD, Comfort ISD and Kendall County offer over-65 and disability tax freezes ([Kendall AD](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)).
- **Counties collecting a farm-to-market or flood-control tax** must give a **$3,000** residence homestead exemption.
- **The 10% cap** applies only once the homestead exemption is in place.

## The January 1 rule nobody tells a relocating buyer

To claim a residence homestead exemption for a tax year, you must have **owned and occupied the home as your principal residence on January 1** of that year ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)).

Close in February and you do not get the exemption for that year. You get it the following year. The application deadline is **before May 1** — commonly stated as April 30.

That has two practical consequences a California buyer should plan around. The first year's tax bill is the unexempted bill, and if the lender escrows from that number the payment is higher than the one you will settle into. The second is that the 10% cap does not protect a property that does not yet carry a homestead exemption, so the first reappraisal after purchase can move a long way, particularly if the prior owner had held the property for years.

Filing the exemption is a form filed with **Kendall Appraisal District**. Nobody files it for you. It is not automatic, it does not carry over from the seller, and the title company does not do it at closing.

## Sales tax, and the part of the bill that is not property

Texas state sales tax is **6.25%**, with local add-ons to a combined maximum of **8.25%**. Boerne is at the maximum: 6.25% state, 1.50% City of Boerne, 0.50% Kendall County ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/646/Current-Tax-Rates)).

If you are buying something to rent out short-term, note that hotel occupancy tax runs **13% total** in Boerne — 6% state plus 7% city — and Boerne has its own short-term rental ordinance that reaches both the city limits and the ETJ.

## The county is growing, which is why reappraisal bites

**Kendall County grew 20.3% between 2020 and 2025**, from an estimated 44,568 to 53,289, driven mostly by domestic migration ([Community Impact](https://communityimpact.com/san-antonio/boerne-fair-oaks-ranch/government/2026/03/30/kendall-county-population-increases-by-203-from-2020-2025/)).

Rising values in a growing county plus annual reappraisal is exactly the mechanism that produces the tax-bill surprise in year two and year three. The protest process exists for this and it has a real deadline. Anyone moving here should know the appraisal notice arrives in spring and the window to protest is short.

## Who answers which question

- **Kendall Appraisal District** — exemptions, appraised value, protests, whether your specific parcel sits in a MUD or WCID.
- **A CPA or tax advisor** — the overall California-versus-Texas comparison, what the move does to your return, and any capital gains question on the California sale.
- **A Texas real estate attorney** — deed restrictions, title, and marital property. Texas is a community property state, which changes how a married couple takes title compared with California's own community property rules.
- **A lender** — how the first-year unexempted tax bill affects the escrow estimate on your loan.

## Related questions

- [Does Texas really have no state income tax, and what do I pay instead?](/answers/does-texas-have-no-state-income-tax)
- [What are property taxes like in Boerne?](/answers/what-are-property-taxes-like-in-boerne)
- [What is the Texas homestead exemption?](/answers/what-is-the-texas-homestead-exemption)
- [What is the 10% homestead cap in Texas?](/answers/what-is-the-10-percent-homestead-cap-in-texas)
- [What surprises out-of-state buyers about buying a house in Texas?](/answers/what-surprises-out-of-state-buyers-about-texas-real-estate)

## Questions about a specific property?

Call or text **[830-446-3847](tel:+1-830-446-3847)** · Email **[heath.shepard@kw.com](mailto:heath.shepard@kw.com)**

---

*This page explains how Texas property and sales taxes are structured. It is not tax or legal advice. For a California-to-Texas comparison on your own numbers, talk with a CPA; for exemptions and appraised value on a specific parcel, contact Kendall Appraisal District.*

question: Should I buy inside Boerne city limits or in unincorporated Kendall County?
metaTitle: Should I buy inside Boerne city limits or in unincorporated Kendall County?
metaDescription: City limits, ETJ or open county: the 0.4716 city rate, well and septic diligence, and the STR ordinance that still reaches Boerne's ETJ.
shortAnswer: Inside the city limits you get City of Boerne utilities and ordinances and pay the city's 0.4716 rate. Unincorporated means well and septic, no city rate, and fewer local rules — except in Boerne's ETJ, where the city still regulates platting and some ordinances, such as short-term rentals, still reach you.
body:
## There are three zones, not two

Almost everyone frames this as city versus country. There are actually three:

1. **Inside the City of Boerne city limits.** City utilities, city ordinances, city zoning, city tax rate.
2. **Boerne's extraterritorial jurisdiction (ETJ).** Unincorporated — no city tax rate — but the city keeps regulatory authority over subdivision platting under **Texas Local Government Code Chapter 42**, and some city ordinances explicitly reach out here.
3. **Unincorporated Kendall County outside the ETJ.** County government, deed restrictions, and the groundwater district. No city layer at all.

The middle one is where buyers get surprised, because a property can carry city rules without a city tax bill or city water. Step one for any address: ask the **City of Boerne Planning Department** which of the three it sits in. That answer drives everything below.

## Utilities

**Inside the city limits:** City of Boerne water and sewer. The city's supply comes from three sources — **Canyon Lake surface water through the Guadalupe-Blanco River Authority, Boerne City Lake, and local Trinity Group aquifer wells** ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/FAQ.aspx?QID=315)). Drought restrictions come from the utility; supply risk is the city's to manage.

**Unincorporated:** typically a private well and an on-site septic system. That moves a set of risks onto you that a city customer never thinks about:

- **Well yield, tested** — gallons per minute, not the seller's recollection.
- **Depth, casing and pump age.**
- **Septic system type, capacity, permit history and last service.** Capacity is sized to bedroom count; adding bedrooms can require a system change.
- **Permitting and pumping limits** under the **Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District**, which regulates groundwater countywide and sets drought stages using roughly 42 monitor wells, stream gauges on Cibolo Creek and the Guadalupe River, and 100-plus rain gauge sites ([ccgcd.org](https://ccgcd.org/)).
- **Shared wells and shared access roads**, both of which live or die on the recorded agreement.

A standard home inspection does not evaluate a well or certify a septic system. Budget separate specialists inside the option period.

## Which taxing entities bill you

The **City of Boerne 2025 rate was 0.4716 per $100** of taxable value ([Kendall County](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/297/Boerne-City-of)). Outside the city limits, that line does not appear. That is the single clearest financial difference, and it is a trade — you are also not buying city water, sewer, trash service or city police response.

Everything else carries across:

- **Kendall County 2025: 0.377** — M&O 0.317976 plus debt 0.059024 ([Kendall County](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/306/Kendall-County)).
- **School district.** **Boerne ISD 2025: 1.0109** (M&O 0.6969 + debt 0.3140) ([Kendall County](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/295/Boerne-ISD)). The western part of the county is **Comfort ISD, 2025 adopted 0.9328** ([Kendall County](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/300/Kendall-County)). Unincorporated does not mean no school district — it means confirm which one.
- **Special districts.** Kendall AD lists **Kendall County MUD, Miralomas MUD, the Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District and Kendall County WCID #1** among entities that can appear on a bill ([Kendall Appraisal District](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)). A MUD rate in a newer subdivision can erase the savings from dropping the city rate.

Pull the entity list for the exact parcel from **Kendall Appraisal District**. That is also where the homestead exemption and any protest get filed for Kendall County property — not Bexar CAD.

Two TREC forms exist because this catches people: the **Notice to Purchaser of Special Taxing or Assessment District (form 59-0, effective 02/12/2024)** and the **Addendum Containing Notice of Obligation to Pay Improvement District Assessment (form 53-0, effective 09/01/2021)** ([TREC contracts](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/contracts)).

## What the city still controls in the ETJ

Boerne's **short-term rental ordinance, No. 2023-09, applies in the city limits and the ETJ** ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/2444/Short-Term-Rentals); [Ordinance 2023-09](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/DocumentCenter/View/23223/Short-Term-Rental-Ordinance-2023-09)). An ETJ property still needs the **$200 two-year permit**, still owes hotel occupancy tax, and still faces the ordinance's requirements — though the **safety inspection is not required for ETJ properties**.

That is the model to hold in your head: unincorporated does not mean unregulated, and the boundary of a city's authority is not the same as the boundary of its tax rate. Subdivision platting in the ETJ runs through the city under Chapter 42, which matters enormously if you intend to split a tract.

**A property in unincorporated Kendall County outside both the city limits and the ETJ is not covered by the Boerne ordinance.** Texas counties have narrower ordinance-making authority than cities, but that is not the same as none. Confirm any specific requirement with **Kendall County** rather than assuming an acreage parcel is rule-free.

## Where deed restrictions take over

Outside the city, private restrictions do the work zoning does inside it. A recorded declaration and a property owners' association can be more restrictive than any city code — on building materials, setbacks, outbuildings, livestock, RVs, rentals and resale.

Texas Property Code Chapter 207 requires an association to provide **subdivision information, including a resale certificate**, on proper written request, covering assessments, unpaid amounts, certain known violations, insurance, certain pending lawsuits, reserves, budgets and transfer restrictions ([Tex. Prop. Code §207.003](https://codes.findlaw.com/tx/property-code/prop-sect-207-003/)). Delivery is within **10 business days** of the written request, and the certificate must be prepared no earlier than **60 days** before delivery. The relevant TREC forms are the **Addendum for Property Subject to Mandatory Membership in a POA (36-11)** and **Subdivision Information, Including Resale Certificate (37-5)** ([TREC](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/contracts)).

Order it early and read it during the option period. A **Texas real estate attorney** is the right person to tell you what a specific set of restrictions permits — that is a legal reading, not an agent's call.

## If the land carries an ag valuation

Much unincorporated acreage sits under **1-d-1 open-space appraisal**, valued on **productivity value** rather than market value. Qualification requires current principal agricultural use to the degree of intensity generally accepted in the area, with agricultural or timber production in **5 of the preceding 7 years**; a wildlife management valuation requires previously qualified land used in **at least 3 of 7** specified ways. Changing the use triggers a **3-year rollback tax** — the difference between taxes paid on ag value and what would have been paid on market value ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/ag-timber/index.php)).

The buy-a-ranchette-and-build failure mode is exactly this: a low carrying cost converts into a rollback bill. Ask **Kendall Appraisal District** whether the valuation survives your intended use, and a **CPA** what the consequence costs.

## How to decide

Buy **inside the city limits** if you want city water and sewer, a shorter commute to everything, predictable utility service, and zoning that governs what your neighbor can build. Pay the 0.4716 for it.

Buy **unincorporated** if you want land, distance and fewer municipal rules, and you are prepared to own the well, the septic, the road agreement and the groundwater question personally.

Either way, before the option period ends: confirm the zone with the **City of Boerne Planning Department**, the taxing entities with **Kendall Appraisal District**, the current drought stage at [ccgcd.org](https://ccgcd.org/), and the recorded restrictions with a **Texas real estate attorney**.

question: What is the Texas disabled veteran property tax exemption?
metaTitle: What is the Texas disabled veteran property tax exemption?
metaDescription: The $5,000 to $12,000 ladder under Tax Code 11.22, the total homestead exemption under 11.131, Form 50-114 by April 30, and surviving spouse rules.
shortAnswer: Texas gives disabled veterans a fixed dollar exemption off one property's appraised value, scaled to the VA disability rating and starting at $5,000 for a 10-29% rating. A veteran rated 100% disabled, or determined individually unemployable, gets a total exemption on their residence homestead under Tax Code 11.131.
body:
## There are two different exemptions, and the difference is enormous

Texas veterans routinely conflate these. They are not the same program.

**The partial disabled veteran exemption (Tax Code §11.22)** is a fixed dollar amount off the appraised value of **one property** the veteran owns. It is not limited to a residence homestead. The amount is tied to the VA disability rating ([Texas Comptroller disabled veterans info pack](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/info-pack/disabled-veterans-exemptions.pdf)).

**The 100% disabled veteran exemption (Tax Code §11.131)** is a **total exemption of the total appraised value of the residence homestead** ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/disabledvet-100-faq.php)). Not a dollar amount off the top. The entire appraised value of the homestead, exempt.

A veteran who qualifies for the total exemption and files only the partial one has left the whole thing on the table.

## The partial exemption ladder

The schedule is set by statute. **Texas Tax Code §11.22(a)** exempts a portion of assessed value by disability rating ([Tax Code §11.22](https://codes.findlaw.com/tx/tax-code/tax-sect-11-22/)):

| VA disability rating | Exemption amount |
|---|---|
| At least 10% but less than 30% | $5,000 |
| At least 30% but less than 50% | $7,500 |
| At least 50% but less than 70% | $10,000 |
| 70% or more | $12,000 |

Kendall Appraisal District publishes the same **$5,000 to $12,000** range for the disabled veteran exemption on its adopted exemptions page ([Kendall Appraisal District](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)).

The bands are written as "at least X but less than Y," which matters at the edges. A 30% rating lands in the $7,500 tier, not the $5,000 one. A 70% rating lands in the top tier.

The partial exemption applies to **one property** the veteran designates, and it is the same property across all taxing units. The Comptroller states it plainly: an applicant may claim the exemption on only one piece of property the applicant owned on **January 1**, and the applicant must be a **Texas resident** to qualify for a homestead exemption ([Texas Comptroller disabled veterans info pack](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/info-pack/disabled-veterans-exemptions.pdf)). A veteran who owns a home, a rental and some acreage picks one. The filing deadline is **April 30**.

## The 100% exemption, and the "or" that people miss

Under **Tax Code §11.131**, a veteran qualifies on **either** a 100% disability rating **or** a VA determination of **individual unemployability** — not both ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/disabledvet-100-faq.php)).

That "or" is the single most consequential detail on this page. Veterans rated at less than 100% schedular but receiving compensation at the 100% rate because of individual unemployability regularly assume they do not qualify, because the word on their award letter is not "100%." The Comptroller's FAQ says the determination of individual unemployability qualifies on its own.

The benefit is a **total exemption on the residence homestead** — the total appraised value. On a homesteaded property, that means the exempting units tax nothing.

## How to apply, and the five-year window

The application is **Form 50-114**, filed with the appraisal district. The ordinary deadline is **April 30**, but the 100% disabled veteran exemption may be filed **up to five years after the delinquency date** for the taxes in question ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/disabledvet-100-faq.php)).

Five years back. A veteran who received a qualifying rating years ago and never filed is not necessarily out of luck, and that is an unusually generous late-filing window by Texas property tax standards. The appraisal district will tell you exactly which years are still open on your account.

The partial disabled veteran exemption uses a different form: **Form 50-135**.

For a Boerne or Kendall County property, both go to the **Kendall Appraisal District** at [kendallad.org](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/). Boerne is in Kendall County, not Bexar County, and not in the City of San Antonio. Bexar CAD does not administer exemptions on Kendall County parcels.

A VA rating change is also worth a call to the district. Ratings move, and the exemption follows the rating — but the district does not learn about a change unless something tells it.

## Surviving spouses, and the trap when they move

A surviving spouse of a veteran who qualified for the 100% exemption may continue it if:

- the spouse has **not remarried**,
- the property **was the veteran's residence homestead at the time of death**, and
- it **remains the spouse's residence homestead**.

([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/disabledvet-100-faq.php))

Here is the part that costs money. **If the surviving spouse moves to a different home, the exemption is capped at the dollar value of the last year's exemption on the prior home.** It does not become a fresh total exemption on the new house ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/disabledvet-100-faq.php)).

A surviving spouse who had a fully exempt home appraised at, say, a modest value and moves to a more expensive one carries forward only that prior dollar figure. The rest of the new home's value is taxable. This is a real consideration in downsizing or relocation decisions, and it is almost never mentioned until after the move.

Two other surviving-spouse categories carry a **100% exemption** on the residence homestead, per the Comptroller ([disabled veterans info pack](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/info-pack/disabled-veterans-exemptions.pdf)):

- The surviving spouse of a **service member killed or fatally injured in the line of duty**, if not remarried.
- The surviving spouse of a **veteran who died as a result of a qualifying condition or disease**, if not remarried — **regardless of the veteran's disability rating at death**.

That second one is worth reading twice. The veteran's rating at the time of death does not control it. Families who assume the exemption died with a partial rating should take the question to the appraisal district.

## What the exemption does not do

- It does not exempt you from filing. Nothing here is automatic.
- It does not cover every property you own. The partial exemption is one property; the total exemption is the residence homestead.
- It does not eliminate special assessments that are not ad valorem taxes. What appears on a bill is not always a property tax.
- It is separate from the **VA funding fee exemption** on a VA loan, which is a mortgage cost, not a property tax matter, and is handled through the lender and the VA.

## Practical sequence

1. Pull your current VA rating decision or award letter, including any individual unemployability determination.
2. Call the appraisal district for the county the property sits in and ask which exemption fits and which form applies.
3. File. Free, directly with the district.
4. Confirm the exemption posted on the next notice of appraised value.
5. If a rating changes, tell the district.

Whether a specific veteran, rating or property qualifies is determined by the appraisal district. For the tax consequences of an exemption, an estate, or a surviving spouse's move, talk with a CPA, and take deed and title questions to a Texas real estate attorney.

## Related questions

- [What is the Texas homestead exemption in 2026?](/answers/what-is-the-texas-homestead-exemption)
- [How do I file for a homestead exemption in Kendall County, Texas?](/answers/how-do-i-file-for-a-homestead-exemption-in-kendall-county)
- [What is the Texas over-65 property tax exemption and school tax ceiling?](/answers/texas-over-65-property-tax-exemption-and-school-tax-ceiling)
- [What is the VA funding fee, and who is exempt?](/answers/what-is-the-va-funding-fee-and-who-is-exempt)
- [Why did my Texas property taxes go up?](/answers/why-did-my-texas-property-taxes-go-up)

## Questions about a specific property?

**Heath Shepard is a 100% disabled veteran** and a licensed Texas REALTOR. If VA benefits or the disabled-veteran exemption are part of your purchase, say so up front and he’ll factor them into the numbers.

Call or text **[830-446-3847](tel:+1-830-446-3847)** · Email **[heath.shepard@kw.com](mailto:heath.shepard@kw.com)**

question: What is the Texas over-65 property tax exemption and school tax ceiling?
metaTitle: What is the Texas over-65 property tax exemption and school tax ceiling?
metaDescription: The Texas over-65 exemption and school tax ceiling explained: the additional $60,000, how the freeze works, and how the percentage transfer works when you move.
shortAnswer: Texas homeowners 65 or older get an additional $60,000 school district homestead exemption on top of the general $140,000, plus a school tax ceiling that freezes school taxes at the amount for the year they qualified. Moving transfers the ceiling as a percentage, not a dollar amount, and only if you file for it.
body:
## Two separate benefits, often confused

The age-65 package is really two things, and mixing them up leads to wrong expectations about a tax bill.

**The exemption** is an amount subtracted from taxable value. School districts must grant an **additional $60,000** residence homestead exemption to owners who are 65 or older or who are disabled, on top of the general **$140,000** school district exemption in effect for 2026. Other taxing units may adopt a local option exemption of **at least $3,000** for the same group ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)).

**The ceiling** is a cap on the tax itself, not on the value. A qualifying homeowner's **school district taxes are frozen at the amount for the year the owner qualified**. Appraised value can climb, the school district's rate can climb, and the school portion of the bill does not go above the ceiling amount ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)).

The ceiling only covers the school district portion. City, county and special district taxes are a separate question, answered entity by entity.

## The ceiling can go down but not up

A ceiling is a maximum, not a fixed payment. If rates fall or value falls enough that the calculated school tax comes in below the ceiling, you pay the lower number. The ceiling does not force you to pay more than the actual calculation.

The ceiling can also be raised by **new improvements**. Adding square footage, a casita, a pool, a shop building — the added value is taxed, and the ceiling is adjusted to account for it. Ordinary repairs and maintenance are a different matter from new improvements, and where the line falls on a specific project is a determination the appraisal district makes.

## Which local entities freeze, and which do not

Statewide, the school district ceiling is mandatory. A city or county freeze is a **local option**, and it is not universal across Texas.

In Kendall County, the appraisal district names the **City of Boerne, Boerne ISD, Comfort ISD and Kendall County** as jurisdictions offering over-65 and disability tax freezes ([Kendall Appraisal District](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)). Which entities cover a specific parcel depends on where that parcel sits — inside Boerne city limits versus unincorporated Kendall County is a different set of taxing units, and a MUD or water district on the bill is not part of any of it.

Do not assume a freeze you had in another Texas county follows you. It is adopted locally and applies locally.

## Moving: this is where money gets lost

An over-65 homeowner who sells and buys another Texas home can carry the school tax ceiling to the new home. Two things about how that works surprise nearly everyone:

**It transfers as a percentage, not a dollar amount.** The old ceiling is expressed as a percentage of what the school taxes would otherwise have been, and that percentage is applied to the new home's school taxes. Someone paying a frozen $1,400 on an older home does not get a $1,400 ceiling on a more expensive new home. They get the same proportional reduction ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)).

**It only happens if you file.** The transfer is not automatic and does not follow you by itself. The sequence is:

1. Request a **tax ceiling certificate — Comptroller Form 50-311** — from the appraisal district for the **old** home.
2. File that certificate with the appraisal district for the **new** home.
3. File a **new residence homestead application** on the new home, including the age-65 exemption.

All three. Skipping the certificate is the common failure: the new homestead exemption gets filed, the age-65 exemption gets filed, and the ceiling percentage never transfers because nobody asked the old district for the certificate.

For a Boerne or Kendall County purchase, step 2 and step 3 go to the **Kendall Appraisal District** at [kendallad.org](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/) — not Bexar CAD, because Boerne is in Kendall County and is not part of San Antonio or Bexar County.

## Qualifying, and the January 1 rule

The underlying requirement is the same as any residence homestead exemption: the owner **owned and occupied the home as a principal residence on January 1** of the tax year ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)). Applications are due **before May 1**.

The age-65 exemption has its own well-known wrinkle in practice, and the appraisal district is the right place to confirm how it is applied in your situation: the qualifying event is a birthday, not a calendar year, and districts handle the first year of eligibility according to the statute's terms. Ask them rather than guessing.

## Why the bill can still move

A frozen school tax is not a frozen tax bill. As of September 2026, the **Boerne ISD rate was 1.0109 per $100 of taxable value for 2025** — 0.6969 maintenance and operations plus 0.3140 debt — after 0.9909 in 2024 and 0.9932 in 2023 ([Kendall County](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/295/Boerne-ISD)). Movement in that rate does not push a ceilinged bill above its ceiling. Movement in a **city** or **county** or **MUD** rate, on a parcel where that entity has no freeze, does.

So an over-65 homeowner can hold a rock-steady school tax and still open a larger total bill. The school line is doing its job; a different line moved.

## What the ceiling does at death

A surviving spouse may continue an over-65 ceiling, subject to the statutory conditions on age and continued homestead use. That is a fact-specific determination, and the appraisal district makes it. A Texas real estate attorney is the right person to look at how title is held before the question ever becomes urgent, because how the deed reads at the time of death affects the answer.

## What to actually do

- File for the age-65 exemption when you become eligible, with the appraisal district, free.
- Confirm on the next notice of appraised value that both the exemption and the ceiling posted.
- Before selling and moving within Texas, request Form 50-311 from the old district first.
- Check which non-school entities on your bill offer a freeze — do not assume.

Eligibility, the ceiling amount and the transfer percentage are all determined by the appraisal district. For the tax consequences of any of it, and for planning around a move or an estate, talk with a CPA.

## Related questions

- [What is the Texas homestead exemption in 2026?](/answers/what-is-the-texas-homestead-exemption)

question: What are property taxes like in Boerne, Texas?
metaTitle: What are property taxes like in Boerne, Texas?
metaDescription: Boerne's 2025 rates per $100: Boerne ISD 1.0109, City of Boerne 0.4716, Kendall County 0.377, plus any MUD or WCID line on the parcel.
shortAnswer: For a home inside Boerne city limits in Boerne ISD, the 2025 adopted rates per $100 of taxable value were Boerne ISD 1.0109, City of Boerne 0.4716 and Kendall County 0.377, plus any special district on the parcel. Boerne files with Kendall Appraisal District, not Bexar CAD.
body:
## The 2025 rate stack, per $100 of taxable value

| Entity | 2025 adopted | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **Boerne ISD** | **1.0109** | M&O 0.6969 + debt 0.3140 |
| **City of Boerne** | **0.4716** | applies inside city limits only |
| **Kendall County** | **0.377** | M&O 0.317976 + debt 0.059024 |

Sources: [Boerne ISD rates](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/295/Boerne-ISD), [City of Boerne rates](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/297/Boerne-City-of), [Kendall County rates](https://www.co.kendall.tx.us/306/Kendall-County).

Recent history for the same three:

- **Boerne ISD:** 1.0109 (2025), 0.9909 (2024), 0.9932 (2023), 1.1786 (2022), 1.2046 (2021)
- **City of Boerne:** 0.4716 (2025), 0.4716 (2024), 0.4766 (2023), 0.4510 (2022)
- **Kendall County:** 0.377 (2025), 0.3827 (2024), 0.38270 (2023), 0.38770 (2022), 0.412700 (2021)

Kendall County's 2025 rate of 0.377 was adopted at the **August 26, 2025 Commissioners Court meeting**, against a posted no-new-revenue rate of **0.373981**, and was a decrease from 2024 ([Community Impact](https://communityimpact.com/san-antonio/boerne-fair-oaks-ranch/government/2025/08/27/kendall-county-commissioners-approve-tax-rate-decrease/)).

Note the pattern: rates have generally drifted down while bills have not necessarily followed, because the rate is only half the equation. The other half is appraised value, and Texas reappraises at market annually.

## It is a different appraisal district than San Antonio

**Boerne is in Kendall County.** Your appraisal district is **[Kendall Appraisal District](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)** — kendallad.org. It is not Bexar CAD, and San Antonio's rates and entities have nothing to do with your bill.

Kendall AD is where a Boerne homeowner files a homestead exemption, files a protest, and confirms which taxing units apply to a specific parcel.

## Not every Boerne-area bill has the same entities on it

The three rates above are the common stack for a home inside the city limits in Boerne ISD. Kendall AD lists these as entities that can appear on a Kendall County tax bill:

- **Boerne ISD**
- **Comfort ISD** — 2025 adopted **0.9328**, from 0.9603 in 2024 and 0.9626 in 2023, serving the western part of the county ([Kendall County](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/300/Kendall-County))
- **City of Boerne**
- **Kendall County**
- **Kendall County MUD**
- **Miralomas MUD**
- **Cow Creek Groundwater Conservation District**
- **Kendall County WCID #1**

Source: [Kendall Appraisal District](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/).

Three practical consequences:

1. **A property outside the city limits does not pay the City of Boerne rate.** That is real money, and it is offset by having no city water, sewer or trash service.
2. **A MUD or the WCID can add a line you did not budget for.** MUD rates are parcel-specific and can be substantial in newer subdivisions.
3. **Comfort ISD is not Boerne ISD.** Kendall County contains both.

Pull the entity list for the exact parcel from Kendall AD. Do not reconstruct it from a listing sheet, and do not assume the seller's current bill is what yours will be.

## Exemptions that change the bill

Texas exemptions reduce taxable value before the rate is applied ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/)):

- **School district residence homestead: $140,000**, raised from $100,000 by **Proposition 13**, approved by Texas voters in **November 2025** and implemented by **SB 4 of the 89th Legislature**, effective for tax year **2026**.
- **Local option homestead exemption:** taxing units may offer up to **20 percent** of appraised value, minimum $5,000.
- **County farm-to-market or flood-control:** counties that collect that tax must grant a **$3,000** residence homestead exemption.
- **Age 65 or older, or disabled:** school districts must grant an **additional $60,000**; other units may adopt a local option of at least $3,000.
- **Deadline: before May 1**, and you must have **owned and occupied the home as your principal residence on January 1** of the tax year.

Kendall AD also notes that several local jurisdictions offer over-65 and disability tax **"freezes"** — named: **City of Boerne, Boerne ISD, Comfort ISD and Kendall County** ([Kendall AD](https://kendallad.org/adopted-tax-rates-and-exemptions/)). Kendall AD applies these; confirm which apply to your account with them.

**Disabled veterans.** The partial exemption under Tax Code §11.22 is a fixed dollar amount off appraised value by VA rating — **$5,000** for a rating of at least 10 percent but less than 30 percent, **$7,500** for at least 30 but less than 50, **$10,000** for at least 50 but less than 70, and **$12,000** at 70 percent or more ([Texas Tax Code §11.22(a)](https://codes.findlaw.com/tx/tax-code/tax-sect-11-22/)). It applies to **one property the veteran designates**, and to that same property across all taxing units. A veteran with a **100 percent disability rating or a determination of individual unemployability** may qualify under §11.131 for an exemption of the **total appraised value** of the residence homestead, applied for on **Form 50-114** ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/exemptions/disabledvet-100-faq.php)).

## The caps

- **Homestead cap: 10 percent per year** on net appraised value, and only for property that already carries a homestead exemption.
- **Circuit breaker (Tax Code §23.231): 20 percent** cap for **non-homestead** real property at or below an annually indexed threshold. It was created by **SB 2 (2023)** as a pilot for tax years **2024, 2025 and 2026 and expires December 31, 2026** unless the Legislature renews it ([Travis CAD](https://traviscad.org/circuitbreaker)).

A buyer's first full year is the year this bites. The seller's bill may reflect a homestead exemption and a capped value the new owner does not inherit. Have your **lender** underwrite the escrow payment on a full, unexempted market valuation.

## Protesting

Deadline: **May 15, or 30 days after the appraisal district mails the notice of appraised value, whichever is later** — counted from the **mailing** date, not the day it landed in your mailbox. Notices must go out by **May 1**, or **April 1** for a residence homestead, or as soon as practical after. The notice of protest form is **Comptroller Form 50-132**, though a protest is sufficient if it identifies the property and owner and states dissatisfaction in writing. The appraisal review board must give **at least 15 days** notice of the hearing, and you may appear in person, by phone or videoconference, or by written affidavit ([Texas Comptroller](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/protests/)).

## One more Boerne rate, for completeness

Sales tax in Boerne is **8.25 percent** — 6.25 state, 1.50 City of Boerne, 0.50 Kendall County. Hotel occupancy tax is **13 percent** — 6 state plus 7 city ([City of Boerne](https://www.ci.boerne.tx.us/646/Current-Tax-Rates)).

For the county's own published rate documents, see [Kendall County Tax Rate Information](https://www.kendallcountytx.gov/184/Tax-Rate-Information).

## Related questions

- [Why are homes in Boerne, Texas so expensive?](/answers/why-are-homes-in-boerne-so-expensive)
- [How do I file for a homestead exemption in Kendall County?](/answers/how-do-i-file-for-a-homestead-exemption-in-kendall-county)
- [How do I protest my property taxes in Texas?](/answers/how-do-i-protest-my-property-taxes-in-texas)
- [What is the 10 percent homestead cap in Texas?](/answers/what-is-the-10-percent-homestead-cap-in-texas)
- [Should I buy inside Boerne city limits or in unincorporated Kendall County?](/answers/should-i-buy-in-boerne-city-limits-or-unincorporated-kendall-county)

## Questions about a specific property?

Call or text **[830-446-3847](tel:+1-830-446-3847)** · Email **[heath.shepard@kw.com](mailto:heath.shepard@kw.com)**

question: What are the 2026 conforming and FHA loan limits in Kendall County, Texas?
metaTitle: What are the 2026 conforming and FHA loan limits in Kendall County, Texas?
metaDescription: 2026 conforming and FHA loan limits for Kendall County and Boerne, Texas, the reported MSA figure, and what a loan limit actually governs.
shortAnswer: For 2026 the conforming one-unit baseline is $832,750, with a high-cost ceiling of $1,249,125. FHA's nationwide one-unit floor is $541,287 and ceiling $1,249,125. Kendall County sits in the San Antonio-New Braunfels MSA, whose 2026 FHA one-unit limit is reported at $557,750 — confirm it on HUD's lookup. VA has no limit on full entitlement.
body:
## Conforming (Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac), 2026

The Federal Housing Finance Agency set the 2026 conforming loan limit for a **one-unit property at $832,750**, an increase of **$26,250** over the 2025 limit of **$806,500**. The **high-cost area ceiling is $1,249,125**, which is 150% of the baseline. FHFA announced the values after its third-quarter 2025 house price index showed prices up **3.26% year over year** ([FHFA](https://www.fhfa.gov/news/news-release/fhfa-announces-conforming-loan-limit-values-for-2026)).

The baseline is the number that applies across most of the country; the $1,249,125 ceiling applies only in areas FHFA designates as high-cost. For a conventional one-unit loan in Kendall County, the baseline is the figure to plan against, and your lender confirms the value applied to your specific county at application.

## FHA, 2026

FHA sets limits county by county within a floor and a ceiling. Per **Mortgagee Letter 2025-23**, the **2026 nationwide one-unit floor is $541,287** and the **ceiling is $1,249,125**, effective for case numbers assigned **January 1 through December 31, 2026** ([HUD Mortgagee Letter 2025-23](https://www.hud.gov/sites/dfiles/hudclips/documents/2025-23hsgml.pdf), [HUD announcement](https://www.hud.gov/news/hud-no-25-145)).

The effective-date language is worth reading carefully. FHA limits key off the date the **case number is assigned**, not the contract date and not the closing date. A loan whose case number was assigned in December 2025 sits under the 2025 limit even if it closes in 2026. That distinction has repriced deals.

Kendall County is part of the **San Antonio–New Braunfels metropolitan statistical area**, which is the geography HUD uses to set the FHA limit here. That is the correct MSA for Boerne — Boerne is in **Kendall County**, not Bexar County and not the City of San Antonio, but the FHA limit is set at the MSA level and the MSA spans both.

**The San Antonio–New Braunfels MSA 2026 FHA limits are reported as $557,750 for one unit, $714,000 for two units, $863,100 for three units and $1,072,600 for four units.** That figure comes from a **secondary source** ([LRG Realty, 2026 loan limits](https://lrgrealty.com/lrg-blog/2026-loan-limits-san-antonio-austin-killeen/)), not from HUD directly, and it has not been confirmed against the official table. **Verify it on HUD's own FHA mortgage limits lookup before relying on it** ([HUD FHA mortgage limits lookup](https://entp.hud.gov/idapp/html/hicostlook.cfm)). Your lender will pull it from that same source when the case number is assigned.

## VA, 2026

There is no dollar figure to look up. Veterans with **full entitlement have no VA loan limit**, and the **VA guaranty does not exceed 25%** of the loan ([U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs](https://www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans/loan-limits/)).

Full entitlement is the condition, not the assumption. A veteran with an active VA loan, or with a prior VA loan that ended in foreclosure or a deed in lieu, may hold only partial entitlement, and in that case entitlement math does constrain the loan. The Certificate of Eligibility resolves it, and the lender pulls it as a matter of course.

"No VA loan limit" also does not mean unlimited borrowing. The VA is declining to cap the loan amount. Income, assets, credit and the appraised value still govern, and the lender still has to approve the file.

## What a loan limit actually governs

A loan limit is an **agency eligibility line**, not an affordability statement and not a price cap on the house.

Below the applicable limit, the loan is **agency-eligible**: Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac can buy a conventional loan, or FHA can insure an FHA loan. That eligibility is why those loans price the way they do — there is a deep, liquid secondary market for them and the pricing reflects it.

Above the limit, a conventional loan becomes a **jumbo**. Nobody is buying it under agency guidelines, so the individual lender or its private investor sets the terms: its own down payment requirement, its own reserve requirement, its own credit standard, its own rate. Jumbo terms vary far more between lenders than conforming terms do, because there is no common rulebook. Two jumbo quotes on the same file can look like two different products.

The practical consequence for a Boerne or Kendall County buyer: the limit is a **threshold in the loan amount, not the purchase price**. A purchase above the limit can still be a conforming loan if the down payment brings the loan amount under it. That is a real planning lever, and it is worth running both ways with a lender — the jumbo option versus a larger down payment that keeps the loan conforming — before assuming the higher-priced structure is required.

## What moves these numbers, and when

Conforming limits are reset annually by FHFA based on its house price index, announced in late fall for the following calendar year. FHA limits are reset annually by HUD in a Mortgagee Letter, keyed to the conforming baseline and set per county with the floor and ceiling as bounds. Both are calendar-year numbers.

Anything on this page is correct **as of September 2026** and is subject to the next annual reset. Before writing an offer near a limit, have your lender confirm the current figure and, for FHA, when the case number will be assigned.

## How this shows up in the contract

A Texas buyer whose purchase depends on a mortgage uses the **Third Party Financing Addendum, TREC form 40-11, effective 01/03/2025** ([TREC contract forms](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/contracts)). TREC promulgates the form and license holders are required to use it; a license holder may not draft contract language. The financing terms written into that addendum should match what your lender has actually approved — not what you hope to qualify for.

## Who to ask

County-level FHA limits come from **HUD's lookup tool** and from your lender at case-number assignment. Entitlement questions go to the **VA** and your lender. Whether a jumbo or a larger down payment is the better structure for your file is a **lender** question, and it is worth asking for both scenarios in writing. Contract language is for a **Texas real estate attorney**.

- [How much down payment do I need to buy a house in Texas?](/answers/how-much-down-payment-do-i-need-in-texas)

question: What credit score do I need to buy a house in Texas?
metaTitle: What credit score do I need to buy a house in Texas?
metaDescription: Why there is no single credit score answer in Texas: agency minimums vs. lender overlays, how score prices a loan, and what a real preapproval is worth.
shortAnswer: There is no single number. Each loan program sets an agency minimum, and then the individual lender adds its own stricter overlay — the overlay is what you actually have to meet. Score also prices the loan and the mortgage insurance, not just approval. Get a real preapproval from a lender who pulls credit and reads your income documents.
body:
## There are two different minimums, and most articles only tell you about the wrong one

Every page that answers this question with a single number is quoting a **program minimum** — the floor published by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac for conventional loans, by HUD for FHA, or by the VA for VA loans. That floor describes what the agency will insure, guarantee or buy. It does not describe what any actual lender will lend you.

On top of the program floor, individual lenders impose **overlays**: their own stricter requirements, set by their risk appetite, their investor relationships and their servicing capacity. Overlays vary lender to lender, they change without notice, and they are not published anywhere you can look them up. A borrower who is comfortably above the program floor can still be declined by one lender and approved by the next one on the same file with the same score.

That is why the honest answer is structural rather than numerical. The number that governs your file is the overlay at the specific lender you apply with, on the day you apply. The only way to learn it is to apply.

## Score is a price, not just a gate

The second thing the single-number framing hides: credit score is mostly a **pricing input**. Approval is binary. Cost is a slope.

Score feeds into loan-level pricing adjustments on conventional loans, which move your interest rate or your closing costs up or down. It feeds into what private mortgage insurance costs on a conventional loan with less than twenty percent down, because the mortgage insurance company is separately underwriting you. On an FHA loan the mortgage insurance structure is set by HUD rather than by your score, which is part of why FHA can pencil out better than conventional for a borrower with a thinner file — and worse for a borrower with a strong one.

So "do I qualify" is the wrong first question. The right one is: **at my score, across the programs I am eligible for, what does the monthly payment actually come out to?** Two loans that both approve can differ meaningfully in what you pay every month for thirty years. A lender can price conventional, FHA and VA side by side on the same file. Ask for that comparison in writing.

## Which score the lender is even looking at

Mortgage underwriting does not use the free score in your banking app. Lenders pull a tri-merge report from all three bureaus, each with its own score, and standard practice is to use the middle of the three for a single borrower. On a joint application, the lower borrower's middle score typically governs. That means the number you have been watching is frequently not the number that decides your loan, and it is often not even close.

Pulling credit costs money and takes a few minutes. Any lender who tells you what you qualify for without pulling it is guessing, and you should treat their answer as a guess.

## What actually makes a preapproval worth anything

A preapproval is only as strong as the work behind it. There is a wide range under the same word:

- A **prequalification** is a conversation. Someone typed your stated income and stated debts into a calculator. It proves nothing.
- A **preapproval** should mean credit has been pulled and the loan officer has read pay stubs, W-2s or tax returns, and asset statements, and has run the file through automated underwriting.
- An **underwritten preapproval** means a human underwriter has reviewed the file and issued conditions. This is the strongest thing a buyer can walk in with short of a cash offer.

The difference matters most on the days it matters most. When a seller is holding two offers, the financing behind them is the tiebreaker, and a letter that says "subject to verification of all information" does not read the same as one from a lender who can say on the phone that the file has cleared underwriting.

## What the seller's side is actually reading

In a Texas contract, a buyer whose purchase depends on getting a mortgage uses the **Third Party Financing Addendum, TREC form 40-11, effective 01/03/2025** ([TREC contract forms](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/contracts)). It is a promulgated form — TREC writes it, license holders are required to use it, and license holders may not draft their own contract language.

That addendum, plus the preapproval letter attached to the offer, is what the listing side evaluates when it weighs your offer against another one. Listing agents call lenders. The answer they get — whether the loan officer picks up, whether they know the file, whether they will speak to the underwriting status — moves offers. A strong file communicated badly loses to a weaker file communicated well more often than buyers expect.

## Credit is a moving target, and mid-contract is the worst time to move it

Your file gets re-verified before closing. Common ways buyers damage their own deal after going under contract:

- Financing furniture or appliances for the new house.
- Opening a store card for the discount at checkout.
- Buying or leasing a vehicle.
- Moving money between accounts without a paper trail, which creates unsourced deposits the underwriter has to chase.
- Paying off and closing an old account, which can shorten average account age.
- Changing jobs, changing from salary to commission, or going from W-2 to 1099.

None of these are hypothetical. All of them have killed loans in the last week before closing. The rule from contract to funding is boring on purpose: change nothing, buy nothing, move nothing, tell the lender first.

## One Texas-specific thing to know now, not later

If you ever plan to pull equity out of the home once you own it, Texas is different from most states. A cash-out refinance or home equity loan on a Texas homestead is governed by the **Texas Constitution, Section 50(a)(6)**, which caps total borrowing against the homestead at **80% of fair market value**, requires a **12-day** waiting period before closing, caps most fees at **2%** of loan principal (excluding the appraisal, survey, title insurance premium and title search), is generally **non-recourse**, and allows only **one** such loan at a time with **12 months** between home equity closings ([Texas cash-out rules summarized](https://hurstlending.com/texas-cash-out-refinance-rules-50a6-guidelines/)).

That matters at purchase because the equity cushion you will need later is set by law, not by what a lender is willing to do. Investment property in Texas is not subject to 50(a)(6). A lender can walk you through how it applies to your plans.

## Who to ask

Qualification, rates, programs, overlays and what your specific score prices out to are **lender** questions, and the answer is file-specific. Credit report errors are disputed with the bureaus, and a reputable lender will tell you whether a rapid rescore is worth attempting on your file or whether it is a waste of thirty days. How the contract's financing terms should be written for your situation is a question for your agent and, where the language itself is at issue, a **Texas real estate attorney**.

## Related questions

- [Conventional vs. FHA vs. VA loan in Texas: which one?](/answers/conventional-vs-fha-vs-va-loan-in-texas)
- [What are the 2026 conforming and FHA loan limits in Kendall County, Texas?](/answers/what-are-the-2026-loan-limits-in-kendall-county)
- [What is the Third Party Financing Addendum?](/answers/what-is-the-third-party-financing-addendum)
- [What is a Texas cash-out refinance (50(a)(6))?](/answers/what-is-a-texas-cash-out-refinance-50a6)

question: What does the effective date mean in a Texas real estate contract?
metaTitle: What does the effective date mean in a Texas real estate contract?
metaDescription: The effective date is the last signature delivered, and day zero for the three-day option fee, the option period, financing and title deadlines.
shortAnswer: The effective date is the date the last party signs the contract and that signature is delivered. It is day zero. Every other deadline in a Texas contract counts from it: the option fee delivery, the option period, the financing deadline, title objections and the closing date. A wrong effective date makes every one of them wrong.
body:
## When the effective date happens

Two events have to occur, in order:

1. **The last party signs.** If the buyer signs Tuesday and the seller signs Thursday, Tuesday is irrelevant to the effective date.
2. **That final signature is delivered** to the other party, in the way the contract provides for delivery.

Signature plus delivery. Not acceptance in principle, not a verbal yes, not "we have a deal" over the phone, not the seller's agent saying the seller is signing tonight.

Things that are **not** the effective date and are regularly mistaken for it:

- The date the buyer wrote the offer.
- The date the seller verbally accepted.
- The date the offer was emailed.
- The date the title company opened the file.
- The date the earnest money was wired.

The effective date is a blank on the contract, filled in when both conditions are met. Under Texas real estate practice it is normally filled in and dated by the broker or agent who receives that last delivery, and it is the one blank on the form that should never be guessed at.

## Why it is the most load-bearing date in the deal

The TREC contract expresses almost nothing as an absolute calendar date. It expresses obligations as **a number of days after the effective date**. Move the effective date by one day and the entire chain slides.

What hangs off it, with the paragraph of the One to Four Family Residential Contract (Resale) that puts it there ([TREC form 20-19, PDF](https://www.trec.texas.gov/sites/default/files/pdf-forms/20-19_4.pdf)):

- **¶5A — earnest money and option fee.** "**Within 3 days after the Effective Date**, Buyer must deliver to [Escrow Agent] ... as earnest money and ... as the option fee." They "**may be paid separately or combined in a single payment**." Delivery is to the escrow agent — the title company, not the seller ([TREC](https://www.trec.texas.gov/article/changes-delivery-option-fee-0)).
- **¶5A(1) — additional earnest money**, delivered within a stated number of days after the Effective Date.
- **¶5B — the option period.** The seller grants the buyer "the **unrestricted right to terminate** this contract by giving notice of termination to Seller within [ ] days after the Effective Date of this contract (Option Period)," with notices due "**by 5:00 p.m. (local time where the Property is located)**." Counted in calendar days with the effective date as day zero — a ten-day option period on a November 1 effective date runs out at 5:00 p.m. on November 11 ([Texas Real Estate Research Center](https://trerc.tamu.edu/article/option-period-basics-2360/)).
- **¶6C — the survey.** Whichever of the three survey boxes is checked, it runs on a stated number of days, and two of the three outcomes back up against "**no later than 3 days prior to Closing Date**."
- **¶7B — the seller's disclosure notice**, delivered within a stated number of days after the Effective Date when box (2) is checked.
- **The financing deadline** under the **Third Party Financing Addendum, form 40-11, effective 01/03/2025**. The contract cross-references it in ¶6C(2): a buyer who elects to obtain the survey and fails to "**may not terminate** the contract under Paragraph 2B of the Third Party Financing Addendum because the survey was not obtained" ([TREC contract forms](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/contracts)).
- **¶6B and ¶6D — the title commitment and the objection window.** 6B runs 20 days from when the **Title Company receives a copy of the contract**, which is a different trigger — and a file that does not get opened on day one has already burned days.
- **HOA subdivision information**, where the association has up to 10 business days from a written request, which itself has to start early.
- **Closing**, stated as a date but negotiated against that whole chain.

One date, nine or more downstream obligations. It is the closest thing a Texas contract has to a single point of failure.

## What the contract says about missing those dates

Three sentences from Paragraph 5 decide most disputes about timing.

**¶5D — no option fee, no option.** "If **no dollar amount is stated** as the option fee or if Buyer fails to deliver the option fee within the time required, **Buyer shall not have the unrestricted right to terminate** this contract under this paragraph 5." A blank and a late delivery produce the same result.

**¶5C — late earnest money.** The seller may terminate or exercise remedies under Paragraph 15, or both, by giving notice to the buyer **before the buyer delivers the earnest money**. The window closes when the money lands, which is why a seller who wants to act on it has to act quickly.

**¶5E — time.** "**Time is of the essence** for this paragraph and strict compliance with the time for performance is required." That is the whole doctrine in one line. There is no substantial-compliance argument built into Paragraph 5.

Two mechanical details that go with them. **¶5A(3)**: funds received are applied "**first to the option fee, then to the earnest money, and then to the additional earnest money**" — so a combined payment that is short leaves the earnest money underfunded rather than the option fee. And **¶5A(4)**: the buyer authorizes the escrow agent to release the option fee to the seller "at any time without further notice to or consent from Buyer," and "**the option fee will be credited to the Sales Price at closing**."

## The weekend rule is narrower than people think

**¶5A(2)** provides that if the last day to deliver the earnest money, the option fee or the additional earnest money falls on a **Saturday, Sunday or Legal Holiday**, the time is extended to the end of the next day that is not one of those. The form defines Legal Holiday by statute: a legal holiday described in **Sections 662.003(a) and 662.003(b)(4) and (6), Texas Government Code**.

Note what that rule covers. It is written into Paragraph 5, about delivery of those funds. It is not a general "all deadlines roll to Monday" rule for the whole contract. The option period itself runs on calendar days and expires at 5:00 p.m. on its final day.

Different clocks in the same contract: calendar days for the option period, the 5A(2) rollover for fund delivery, business days for the HOA's 10-day response, and "the earlier of the Closing Date or X days" for title objections. Mixing them up produces a confident wrong answer.

## What actually goes wrong

**Backdating to "make the numbers work."** Someone writes an earlier date so the option period lines up with a weekend, or because the offer was made days earlier. That is not a scheduling convenience. It is a misstatement on an executed contract, it can start deadlines that have already run, and it can hand a party a defense they would not otherwise have.

**Guessing forward.** Someone fills in the date the seller *plans* to sign. If the seller signs later, the contract now says deadlines began before it existed.

**Leaving it blank.** A contract circulating with no effective date has no computable deadlines. Nobody knows when the option fee is due, which means it gets delivered late, which means the buyer loses the unrestricted termination right entirely — the single most common way a Texas buyer forfeits protection they paid for.

**A multi-party signature that never got delivered.** Two sellers, one signs, the other's page is signed but never sent. No delivery, no effective date, and everyone proceeds as though the clock is running.

## If the date on the contract is wrong

Do not fix it by writing over it. Changing a date on an executed contract is changing a contract term, and Texas contracts are changed one way: an **Amendment to Contract, form 39-11, effective 07/01/2026**, signed by every party and delivered ([TREC contract forms](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/contracts)).

If deadlines have already run against the wrong date, the situation is no longer a clerical question and the parties' rights may already have been affected. That is a question for a **Texas real estate attorney**, not something to solve by agreement in a group text.

## The habit that prevents all of it

The moment the contract goes effective, build the deadline calendar from that date and send it to everyone — buyer, seller, lender, title company, inspector.

- Option fee delivered to the title company, and confirmation from the title company that it was received.
- Option period expiration, with the time: 5:00 p.m. local.
- Financing approval deadline.
- Title commitment review and objection deadline.
- HOA document request date, and the 10-business-day outside date.
- Closing date.

The contract for an ordinary resale is **form 20-19, effective 07/01/2026** ([TREC](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/one-four-family-residential-contract-resale)); condominiums, builder new construction and farm and ranch use their own promulgated contracts, and the day counts live in the same place on each.

Every deadline in that list is enforceable against a party who misses it, and none of them send a reminder.

## Related questions

- [What is the option period in a Texas real estate contract?](/answers/what-is-the-option-period-in-texas)
- [How does the option fee work in Texas?](/answers/how-does-the-option-fee-work-in-texas)
- [What is the Third Party Financing Addendum in Texas?](/answers/what-is-the-third-party-financing-addendum)
- [What is the TREC 1-4 Family Residential Contract?](/answers/what-is-the-trec-1-4-family-residential-contract)
- [What is the Amendment to Contract in a Texas real estate deal?](/answers/what-is-the-amendment-to-contract-form-in-texas)

## Questions about a specific property?

Call or text **[830-446-3847](tel:+1-830-446-3847)** · Email **[heath.shepard@kw.com](mailto:heath.shepard@kw.com)**
